articles.title: 2026 Mr. Olympia Live Updates, Highlights and Reaction From Night 2
articles.summary: Will the next Arnold Schwarzenegger please stand up?
articles.body:
A two-day gauntlet of callouts, confirmations and competition ended in the wee hours of Sunday morning (on the East Coast) for the final field of 10 athletes in the Men's Open (Mr. Olympia) division before Nick Walker edged Samson Dauda and earned his first title.

Dauda had won previously in 2024. Two-time champion Derek Lunsford, who won in 2023 and 2025, dropped from first last year to third this year.

Walker, who also won a Peoples Champion title determined by online voting, edged a top-five field in Las Vegas that also included Andrew Jacked in fourth and Tonio Burton in fifth.

"I'm speechless," an emotional Walker said.

"(My coach) brought me back to life. He made this fun for me again. And I don't think I'd be in this position without him."

articles.title: Florida drops impressive offensive performance to pull off massive win over No. 4 Ole Miss
articles.summary: The Florida Gators stunned No. 4 Ole Miss in the Swamp with a dominant ground game as two running backs each rushed for over 100 yards in the win.
articles.body: After one of the most emotionally intense games of the season against their former coach Lane Kiffin and LSU, Ole Miss traveled down to the Swamp to take on the Florida Gators. Sure, the intensity going into the game was nothing like the week before, but Florida was always going to be a challenge, coming in as the No. 21 team in the nation, with Ole Miss showing up in Gainesville at No. 4. However, in the early going, it was all Florida. JON SUMRALL SHARES HILARIOUS RESPONSE TO HEARING HIS FLORIDA TEAM IS FAVORED AGAINST OLE MISS Gators running back Jadan Baugh opened the scoring with a short run to the end zone. Kicker Patrick Durkin tacked on the extra point and hung another three points on the board with a field goal later in the quarter. Ole Miss finally got their zero off the board with a field goal early in the second quarter and another late. FLORIDA GATORS, OLE MISS REBELS FIND THEMSELVES IN GOOD OLD-FASHIONED 'RESPECT OFF' AHEAD OF SATURDAY'S GAME Unfortunately for Ole Miss, those two field goals sandwiched another rushing touchdown for Baugh, and the Gators took a 17-6 lead to the locker room at halftime. The second half is when the offense really started to heat up. Ole Miss signal caller Trinidad Chambliss scored a rushing touchdown on the team's first drive of the half. However, Florida answered right back with a rushing touchdown from running back Duke Clark. It was all about the ground game. Florida posted 302 rushing yards, with both Baugh and Clark rushing for over 100 yards apiece, making it the first time two Gators have done that in the same game since 2022. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Florida led the entire game and really pulled away in the fourth quarter, which saw the lone passing touchdown of their seven trips to the red zone on the day. The Gators offense has been impressive, putting up more than 50 points in all but one game this season, but this was one that is really going to get them some attention ... That one game where they failed to hit the 50-point mark? That was last weekend against Auburn, in which they scored a paltry 44 points. Florida hadn't beaten a top-5 team since a win over Georgia in 2020, and there's no doubt that this win is going to shake up the rankings. articles.title: Giants see best of Camilo Doval in his return, but Dodgers prevail
articles.summary: Former San Francisco Giants closer Camilo Doval, back with the team, struck out the side in a one-inning appearance Saturday. Unfortunately for the Giants, t...
articles.body:
Camilo Doval returned to the Oracle Park mound for the first time since being traded to the Yankees last year, and wow - what a reintroduction for the former San Francisco Giants closer.

The prodigal right-hander hit 99.5 mph with his fastball and struck out Mookie Betts , Shohei Ohtani and Dalton Rushing in the seventh inning of San Francisco 's 4-3 loss to the Dodgers; the Giants tied it up in the eighth on Bo Davidson's sacrifice fly, but Kiké Hernández 's homer off Trent Harris in the ninth provided the difference.

The Giants are a major-league worst 16-29 in one-run games after Saturday, one reason the team needs to bolster the bullpen - making Doval all the more intriguing.

Walks helped hasten Doval's departure last year, as he at times struggled throwing strikes, so the Ks are impressive. But as the Giants determine whether he's part of their plans next year, they'll have to be convinced he can throw strikes consistently. San Francisco's first order of business this winter is to improve the late-inning options, though, so Doval's velocity, and his success against the top of the L.A. order, won't hurt his chances, nor will his eagerness to pitch for the Giants.

With Doval's appearance Saturday, the Giants tied the 2025 Braves for most players used in a season, with 71.

They have a shot at setting the all-time record Sunday if catcher Zach Morgan, still on the taxi squad, makes his debut. Manager Tony Vitello has said repeatedly that he would like to get Morgan into a game after two stints on the roster without being used.

With all this roster upheaval, the idea this final month is to find possible keepers for next season, and among other things, the Giants have found a young pitcher who likes to face the Dodgers. Matt "Tugboat" Wilkinson jumped into the rivalry with five scoreless innings last Sunday and three innings Saturday in which he allowed just a solo homer by Betts.

After he left the game, things shifted slightly, Los Angeles scoring twice in the fourth off Duncan Davitt, while Blake Snell , the onetime Giants starter, held his old team down with little fuss in his four innings. San Francisco, shut out the night before in Tarik Skubal 's start, got a sacrifice fly from Turner Hill in the fourth and nothing more until Drew Cavanaugh's pinch-hit RBI triple in the seventh.

Cavanaugh also dunked a two-out, two-strike double down the third-base line in the ninth, but Tanner Scott struck out Christian Koss to end it.

Briefly: Left-hander Seth Lonsway was promoted from Triple-A Sacramento, with the Giants optioning out Friday night starter Yunior Marte . A sixth-round pick in 2021, Lonsway had a 5.11 ERA in 24 outings with Triple-A Sacramento but he's had good numbers against lefties, who hit him at a .218 rate this year. ... Going into Sunday's finale, San Francisco is a season-high 31 games under .500 and trying to avoid a Dodgers sweep and prevent L.A. from winning 100 games.

articles.title: Browns-Panthers fantasy and prop bets: Bet on Judkins, Judkins, and more Judkins
articles.summary: Are you ready to gamble on a breakout day for Quinshon Judkins?
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are at home against the Carolina Panthers in Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season this Sunday, September 27, at 1:00 pm ET. The Browns are 2.5-point underdogs against the Panthers, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Here are my favorite player prop bets from the Browns' perspective in Week 3.

We took the over on TE Harold Fannin having 36+ receiving yards. He had 54.

We took the over on QB Deshaun Watson having 176+ passing yards. He had 238.

The one we lost was that we also had the over on RB Raheim Sanders having 9+ rushing yards. We might have been a little too cute with that one, as he only finished with 4 rushing yards.

Browns vs. Panthers Best NFL player prop bets

We're starting bold this week. To clarify, if you take this bet, it means that not only will RB Quinshon Judkins score a touchdown, but it will also be the first touchdown scored by either team in the game.

With the Panthers' run defense having been gashed a bit over these first two weeks, and Cleveland showing a trend of taking the ball first on offense, it's not a bad gamble that Judkins will find his way into the end zone for the first time this season. The risk here is the fact that the Browns' offense has historically struggled to get points in the first half of games under Watson.

Quinshon Judkins Most Rushing Yards (+130)

We're really riding the Judkins' breakout game hard this week. Chubba Hubbard hasn't lit it up for Carolina either. Even though Deshaun Watson has been the Browns' leading rusher this season, the idea here obviously is that Judkins can get close to the 100-yard rushing mark. For practical senses, this bet comes down to who you think will have more rushing yards between Hubbard and Judkins.

Quinshon Judkins Over 59.5 Rushing Yards (-113)

Why not keep it simple? This is probably the first time that I've ever done the hat trick of having three best bets on the same player. But if Judkins is going to achiever either of the first two, then logic says he'll also hit the over on 60+ yards rushing. For reference, four players in two games against the Panthers have had 60+ yards rushing.

articles.title: Players of the game from FSU's win over Central Arkansas
articles.summary: Florida State's 34-7 win over Central Arkansas was good, but who were the players of the game?
articles.body:
The Florida State Seminoles defeated the Central Arkansas Bears 34-7 on Saturday in Doak Campbell Stadium. Ahead of a tough ACC schedule, this was a necessary confidence booster for everyone from the players to the coaches.

The Seminoles' offense was without question the bright spot of the day, with 179 rushing yards and 238 yards through the air. Ousmane Kromah was the star of the show, even without his top running mate in Samuel Singleton Jr. , and finished the game with two of FSU's four touchdowns.

With all of this in mind, here are our players of the game.

No question, Kromah was a bright spot of the offense, going for 86 yards and two touchdowns on 11 carries, averaging an efficient 7.8 yards per carry. If he can keep doing that against the upcoming ACC schedule, there is no question that the Seminoles have a fighting chance against their upcoming gauntlet.

Boggs had a great day as well , going for 122 yards on 6 receptions for a touchdown and being the given of breaking the rock after the win. He was perfect, catching all of the balls thrown his way today. A 34-yard touchdown helped put the game far out of reach, giving FSU a 31-7 lead in the third quarter.

Robinson's score on the three-play touchdown drive was electric and set the tone early. While his numbers aren't as eye-popping as one would expect from the preseason All-American (13 catches for two touchdowns and 262 yards), he was a key contributor in the win.

Two field goals and four extra points made for a perfect day for Panikowski. He is exceptionally reliable and hasn't missed a kick all year. Come late in the season, a few losses could be flipped to wins because of him.

articles.title: Brown has a pair of scores, special teams add a score and Auburn edges Vanderbilt 21-15
articles.summary: Byrum Brown threw and ran for a touchdown, Cade Carlson recovered a blocked punt for a score and Auburn beat Vanderbilt 21-15 on Saturday.  The Tigers (3-1,...
articles.body:
AUBURN, Ala. (AP) — Byrum Brown threw and ran for a touchdown, Cade Carlson recovered a blocked punt for a score and Auburn beat Vanderbilt 21-15 on Saturday.

The Tigers (3-1, 1-1 Southeastern Conference) bounced back from a home loss to Florida to give coach Alex Golesh his first league win.

Brown completed 18 of 27 passes for 140 yards, including a touchdown to Chas Nimrod , and threw an interception.

Omar Mabson II added 24 yards rushing and turned in the play of the day on special teams: He blocked a punt in the second quarter that Carlson scooped up and returned 10 yards to put the Tigers ahead 14-3.

Jared Curtis completed 22 of 33 passes for 199 yards for Vandy (3-1, 0-1). He also led the team with 18 carries for 46 yards.

The Commodores got field goals from Brock Taylor on their final two possessions, the last coming with 6:26 to play but the Tigers ran out the flock on the ensuing possession

Vanderbilt: Curtis played mostly mistake-free ball in his first-ever career road start. The true freshman went 22 for 33 for 199 yards, with his only turnover coming off a Hail Mary pass to end the first half. Curtis also led the team in rushing, picking up 48 yards on 18 carries.

Auburn: The Tigers win their first SEC game at home in 671 days. Auburn's defense bounced back, holding Vanderbilt to only 15 points. After giving up 44 points and 495 yards to Florida a week ago, Auburn held the Commodores to 311.

Vanderbilt: At No. 2 Georgia next Saturday.

Auburn: At No. 14 Tennessee next Saturday.

articles.title: Maryland football destroyed by UCLA, 54-3, in 9th straight Big Ten loss
articles.summary: COLLEGE PARK, Md. — Maryland was outclassed from the start. In a game that was scoreless after one quarter but quickly devolved into another lopsided loss, n...
articles.body:
COLLEGE PARK, Md. — Maryland was outclassed from the start.

In a game that was scoreless after one quarter but quickly devolved into another lopsided loss, nothing went the Terps' way. Maryland couldn't establish a running game despite a questionable insistence on doing so; quarterback Malik Washington never got going in the one-dimensional offense and threw four interceptions; and the Terps' defense struggled to stop anything.

All of that led to a 54-3 loss to UCLA and Bob Chesney, Michael Locksley's second straight defeat to a first-year coach after the Terps fell to James Franklin's Virginia Tech last week. Displeasure in the form of "fire Locksley" chants echoed throughout a barren SECU Stadium when the Bruins went up by three touchdowns in the second quarter in what became UCLA's largest conference road win since 1955 and one of the worst losses of Locksley's tenure.

After acknowledging that his team "wasn't good enough," the coach still voiced confidence in his spiraling program's direction.

"Still got a lot of belief in this team, the guys in the locker room," Locksley said. "I won't stop fighting or coaching for them."

Some attention shifted to athletic director Jim Smith after that loss to the Hokies, when Locksley's team wasted another opportunity to prove this season could be different in front of a sold-out crowd. But calls for Smith to make a move will intensify this week after another frustrating result, this time in front of a sparse home crowd during a nor'easter that reflected Terps fans' shrinking confidence in the program's direction.

Maryland is 2-2 after the loss with its next two games on the road at Nebraska and No. 7 Ohio State. The Terps return home in three weeks to take on Rutgers.

"Now isn't time for us to hang our heads," Locksley said. "We've got to do just like we do each week: get back in here tomorrow, figure out what we need to do to get us back on track."

Some things were out of Locksley's control Saturday. Maryland's two leading running backs — DeJuan Williams and Harry Dalton III — and six running backs overall were out with injuries. A player who originally transferred to Maryland to join the baseball team took backup running back snaps in pregame warmups. The backup quarterback took a handoff at one point. Maryland finished with 39 rushing yards on 30 attempts.

"He shouldn't have to feel he needs to carry the team," Locksley said of Washington.

That made Maryland's offensive game plan even more confusing. On 16 rushing attempts in the first half, eight of them from third-string back Iverson Howard, the Terps ran for minus-1 yard. In turn, UCLA easily shut down Washington through the air, as he finished 18 for 38 for 142 yards and four interceptions. The Terps' only first-half possession that didn't end in a punt was the sophomore quarterback's first interception of the season, a third-and-22 desperation heave into triple coverage.

"One loss doesn't define our team," Washington said. "Hasn't defined anybody ever. So, we have an opportunity to bounce back. I trust this team and how strong we are as a unit, how collected we are. We're going to stay together and find a way through."

Meanwhile, a Maryland defense that held the Bruins scoreless through the first quarter broke down in the second. UCLA scored touchdowns on three consecutive drives to take a lead its defense held. Each scoring play came on a direct snap to a running back.

Like other losses throughout Locksley's tenure, penalties were an issue. A face mask infraction negated a third-down stop, keeping UCLA's offense on the field on a scoring drive. The Terps were penalized six times for 60 yards.

Self-inflicted mistakes further sunk Maryland in the second half. Washington threw two third-quarter interceptions, both returned for Bruins touchdowns, with the final one putting UCLA up 31. Both teams emptied their benches, and UCLA kept piling on.

Locksley, for the second week in a row, said he was surprised by the result.

"If you come watch the work that they put in Monday through Friday, there's no one that would have expected it," the coach said.

The loss marks Maryland's ninth straight against Big Ten teams after ending last season on an eight-game losing streak. The Terps haven't won a home conference game since upsetting Southern California in 2024, a result that led to a field storming.

It's hard to imagine the fanbase feeling that elated again. Fans made their opinions known Saturday before dispersing at halftime.

With the program's future as murky as Saturday's weather, it's Smith's turn to respond.

articles.title: Kirk Ferentz visibly emotional after miracle Iowa win 'we'll all remember'
articles.summary: The 71-year-old knows how special this win was.
articles.body:
In a battle of long-time Big Ten foes, Iowa snatched victory away from Michigan with a last-second, walk-off touchdown to secure a 20-19 win.

The Hawkeyes were down most of the game, but executed a game-winning drive to escape Ann Arbor with the victory. With just two seconds left, Hank Brown found Reece Vander Zee in the corner of the endzone to stun the Michigan crowd.

Iowa's offense struggled for much of the day, but the defense and special teams kept them alive enough for the unit to finally score 13 points in the fourth quarter. Thanks to a few fortunate plays, Iowa took advantage of one final play to walk-off in the Big House.

Head coach Kirk Ferentz has seen a lot of football in his time with the Hawkeyes, so he knows how important road conference games can be. The 71-year-old definitely understood how impressive this win was for his squad.

Here's a look at how Ferentz reacted following this win.

Iowa's miracle win over Michigan put the Hawkeyes at 4-0 on the season, but this win was certainly the most memorable of them all thus far. In his interview with CBS' Jenny Dell after the game, Ferentz was clearly emotional over the result.

"One thing about these guys is they don't quit, they fight" he said.

Then, when Dell asked if Ferentz could if this win could compare to any other in the Big House, the veteran coach said there wasn't another.

"Never one like this, it's one we'll all remember," he added.

Ferentz has been leading Iowa's football team since 1998, and he's battled Michigan in the Big Ten for the last three decades. He is now 8-9 in his career against the Wolverines, but this win was certainly special in the way it came about.

articles.title: Ducks get clarity on roster battles, power play in preseason finale loss to Kings
articles.summary: Nikita Nesterenko and Judd Caulfield made impacts on the fourth line, and Anaheim's top loaded power play unit produced, as Ducks look to figure out regular...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – Mercifully, the Anaheim Ducks preseason is over.

While the negative plays outnumber the positive plays from the last three games of the Ducks preseason slate–all losses, and the last two by a combined 16-2 scoreline–it should be quite easy to put in the rearview mirror next week.

"It's a preseason game," Joel Quenneville said. "We tried a lot of things in the lines again tonight. So we got a week to prepare, and (figure out) the lineup, and then getting set and prepared to start the season on a positive note."

What Anaheim can latch onto in the immediate future are the early results in Saturday's 6-2 loss to the Los Angeles Kings at Crypto.com Arena.

The Ducks' fourth-line opened the scoring with impact from roster hopeful Nikita Nesterenko , and while the Kings' leveled, Anaheim's new look top power play unit played with tenacity and creativity for Beckett Sennecke 's fourth goal of the preseason.

They can also look to correct what came after with a slew of penalties and defensive lapses that let the Kings score five unanswered goals, including two power play markers. Part of the lapses can be chalked up to a young, unsettled and mixed up defensive group, but there are trends that need to be stemmed before it kicks off for real in Vegas next Friday.

"We got to fix our details and some habits, but I think we did some things well," Jackson LaCombe said. "I thought it was good for us. It shows us what we can work on as a group."

"You're obviously building habits that you're gonna take into the regular season," Nesterenko said. "I mean, if you do things not the right way, and then that habit sticks, that's gonna translate, and it's gonna cost points later on during the season."

Here are major takeaways from Saturday's preseason finale:

With AJ Greer still out of the line-up (day-to-day, upper body injury) and Jeff Malott sitting on Saturday (under the weather), there was opportunity for one last impression for the hopefuls on the edge of the Ducks forward group.

Nico Myatovic played third-line left wing with Ryan Poheling and Frank Vatrano , and Nikita Nesterenko and Judd Caulfield got their shots on the fourth line wings around Tim Washe . Each of the three made a case.

Nesterenko and Caulfield had the most high-profile impact on the Ducks' first goal. Washe chipped the puck low, and Caulfield's forecheck won the battle for Anaheim on the boards. Washe fished the puck out and fed Nesterenko in the slot for a clean high finish, 1-0.

"Timmy made an all world play there to find me all in front," Nesterenko said. "Saw the goalie down, and I just had to elevate it. Just putting pucks in, tiring out the D, that's what we have to bring consistently. There's guys on this team that are relied on to score every night, and you just have to know your role and just keep it simple and play the game the coaches want to play."

Caulfield has surprised this preseason and earned his second assist, which paired with his physical play was a great effort put forth by the 6-foot-3, 220-pound 25-year-old. Caulfield has played the last three seasons with the AHL San Diego Gulls with a career-high 17 goals and 38 points last season.

Nesterenko is more familiar to Ducks watchers with 61 games played as a Duck, including 29 games last season.

Myatovic's candidacy was even more of a surprise than Caulfield's, despite Myatovic's pedigree in the organization as a second round pick in 2023. In his second full season in San Diego last year, the 21-year-old scored just seven goals with 12 assists in 71 games.

However, his speed and physicality has proven to be an asset in the preseason. Myatovic used his wheels to draw a penalty and hit the post on a breakaway in that sequence.

When Greer is healthy, there will be two spots for those three forwards, and each has a case to claiming a spot.

Roger McQueen and Sam Colangelo were scratches on Saturday, likely pointing to a start in San Diego.

If the Ducks' blue line is not healthy entering the season, it may be a bigger area of concern than even previously thought.

With Ian Moore (lower-body, 1-3 more weeks) and Drew Helleson (lower body, targeting opening night) already out, Pavel Mintyukov (under the weather) was also not in the line-up on Saturday, which gave Anaheim a nearly full slate of defensive hopefuls to evaluate.

"We got some guys we get back there," Quenneville said. "I think that you get a little clearer on how the lines are gonna start next week. So, but got a couple guys that come back, and a couple guys that might not be ready to start"

Jackson LaCombe and Nick Jensen are making the opening night line-up, and Tristan Luneau has performed as anticipated to earn his spot.

Tyson Hinds has been considered a lock, due to his cracking the roster late last season and in the playoffs, and after entering training camp nursing a lower-body injury, his preseason outings haven't been his best. However, there are caveats.

First, it's hard to blame anyone in particular for the 10-0 drubbing the Ducks prospects took against San Jose 's NHL roster on Thursday, but Hinds was a minus-4 in over 18 minutes of ice time.

On Saturday, the left-handed Hinds played most of the first two periods on his off side to the right of LaCombe on the top pair. Hinds moved back to the left of Luneau on the second pair. Hinds was on the ice for two goals and unable to tie up his man in front on a rebound and a tip-in.

Hinds is still likely in the roster, but Anaheim will need better from him, even in a third pairing capacity.

Stian Solberg has been fairly effective in his preseason outings. Heck, in that San Jose drubbing, he was the only Ducks player to escape without a minus on his ledger.

On the other hand, Solberg hasn't gone above and beyond, and for the 2024 first-round pick, he must be earning playing time to stay in Anaheim. Otherwise, like Luneau before him, his best development path would be to stay in San Diego for that top-pairing ice time.

Travis Mitchell has been considerably fine. If he is in Anaheim, it is strictly as the extra defenseman sitting in the press box or emergency fill in. He has a few games of NHL experience with the New York Islanders and can play both sides.

Where Solberg and Mitchell land depends on the health of Anaheim's blue line.

If Helleson is healthy for opening night, it's likely Mitchell stays in Anaheim to be the seventh defenseman, and Solberg would go to San Diego to play. Once Helleson and Moore are healthy, Mitchell likely also heads to San Diego.

Anaheim showcased a new top power play unit, and now that the roster is consolidated, that group is a fully armed and operational battle station.

"We're going to need our power play to be effective," Quenneville said. "I think there's the quality of the possession and recognition and movement, its high end. We have a lot of things that can develop just by improvising on loose pucks and off of that they can materialize a lot of things. Entries should be all right, but I thought we had a good job. I don't think we even had a (bad) entry tonight."

The Ducks ran out their best players on their best unit. Jackson LaCombe ran the point with Leo Carlsson on the high left flank and Cutter Gauthier on the high right flank. Beckett Sennecke was down low on the left and Mikael Granlund was down low on the right.

However, the key wasn't the positioning but the movement. It was not stagnant in the same way Ducks power play units past can bog themselves down. There was movement in and out and from board to board, as Anaheim battled for puck retrievals.

"I think commitment to detail from all of us," LaCombe said. "Just go into the right spots, battling for pucks, things like that, getting more shots. I think we got better at that towards the end of the year and we just kind of continue from there.

Eventually, Carlsson dug the puck off the left boards back to LaCombe, who dished to Gauthier on the right, who found Carlsson in the middle. Carlsson added one last flip to Sennecke, who was wide open in the left circle with time and space to zing a shot five hole.

Now, it's a top-loaded group, but if it can perform at that kind of efficiency, it'll be a boon for the Ducks hopes to return to the playoffs.

articles.title: Saints elevate two wide receivers for Week 3 home opener vs. Raiders
articles.summary: Two wide receivers are coming up from the New Orleans Saints practice squad for Week 3’s game with the Las Vegas Raiders. For one, it’s the last time.
articles.body:
A couple of wide receivers are coming up from the New Orleans Saints practice squad for Week 3's home opener with the Las Vegas Raiders . For one of them, it's the last time.

Veteran backup Kevin Austin Jr. will be elevated from the practice squad for the third and final time this season on Sunday. NFL rules prohibit teams from calling up a player from the practice squad more than three times in a single season before requiring them to sign with the 53-man roster. Austin has mainly worked as a blocker while offering depth behind Chris Olave , Devaughn Vele , Bryce Lance, and Barion Brown .

He's being joined by Jalen Moreno-Cropper, a journeyman who previously played for the Dallas Cowboys and UFL's Houston Gamblers. With Brown sidelined by a hamstring injury, expect Moreno-Cropper to handle duties in the return game fielding punts and kickoffs. That's something he did during the preseason. Brown made a game-changing play in a big kick return before halftime last week, so let's see if Moreno-Cropper can keep the special teams on point Sunday afternoon.

articles.title: Instant reactions from Florida's home win against Ole Miss in Week 4
articles.summary: Here are the Gators Wire staff's instant reactions and analysis for Florida's big home win against the Ole Miss Rebels in Week 4.
articles.body:
Florida football is off to its first 4-0 start since 2019 after running the Ole Miss Rebels out of Ben Hill Griffin Stadium by a final score of 52-28 on Saturday afternoon.

The Gators got out in front early with a 10-point lead at the end of the first 15 minutes, but the Rebels returned and cut the lead to three heading into the locker room at halftime. The two SEC rivals played tug-of-war in the third quarter before the Orange and Blue took control in the final frame.

Jon Sumrall's squad put on a clinic on the ground, rushing for 302 yards on 52 carries spearheaded by a pair of 100-plus-yard efforts from Jadan Baugh (142 yards on 29 attempts) and Duke Clark (126 yards on 12 attempts). While the defense had some shaky moments, it came through when it mattered, and the special teams had a strong showing in the Swamp.

Immediately after the dust settled on the Week 4 rumble, the Gators Wire staff submitted their instant reactions and analysis to the victory in good, bad and ugly format. Here is what we had to offer.

PHOTOS: Highlights from Florida vs Ole Miss in the Swamp for Week 4

GOOD : Florida's star running back keeps legitimizing the Heisman chatter. Jadan Baugh scored multiple touchdowns in a game for the fourth consecutive time this season and looked every bit as dominant against the No. 4 team in the nation as he did against FCS program Campbell. The Doak Walker Award watchlist honoree totaled 83 yards in the first half alone and found the end zone twice before the break.

Duke Clark responded after Ole Miss cut the lead to three, breaking free for an electric 45-yard dash that lit up the Swamp. Florida responded every time Ole Miss sliced the lead to single digits. Jon Sumrall's team capped the third quarter with an Aaron Philo rushing TD after Montgomery's 74-yard kickoff return.

BAD : Aaron Philo was praised for his accuracy after transferring from Georgia Tech this offseason and it was supposed to be one of the reasons he beat out redshirt freshman Tramell Jones Jr., but it was his lack of precision that raised some concerns on Saturday. Philo's misfires cost the Gators two opportunities to extend the first-half lead.

While Florida ultimately pulled out a victory, it's safe to question whether the team is winning in spite of Philo's deficiencies.

UGLY : Trinidad Chambliss gashed the Gators' secondary to start the second half for a 49-yard bomb that set up the score that cut Florida's lead to three. The Gators' defense provided little resistance on the following possession as Chambliss scored on back-to-back possessions to start the second half. Penalties emerged as something to watch for Brad White's group in the second half as penalties helped propel two Ole Miss scoring drives.

GOOD : Florida's special teams were particularly special on Saturday, gaining a total of 264 return yards on six chances and scoring 10 points on field goals and extra points — going perfect on all eight total attempts.

London Montgomery had a monster day, returning three kicks for 128 yards with a longest run of 74 yards, while Alec Clark brought back a pair of punts for a total of 113 yards with a longest return of 70 yards. Maybe even more impressive is that Vernell Brown III — who had been the big name on the unit in previous games — did not get a single touch.

Those returns shortened the field significantly for the Gators' offense, which was critical in their success given Philo's continued struggles with downfield passes.

BAD : Inability to contain Chambliss on the ground made this game a lot closer than it should be in the middle minutes, allowing him to scamper a total of 44 yards on seven carries for a pair of scores, with many runs through wide-open holes in the defensive line.

Florida also managed just one sack, but the corps does get a gold star for the forced fumble out of Chambliss' hand. Still, quarterbacks with even a modicum of mobility seem to be a bit of an Achilles heel for Brad White's squad.

UGLY : Penalties again reared their ugly head, and while it was not quite as egregious as last weekend against Auburn, the yellow flag killed some big plays and gave Ole Miss more opportunities than it deserved. Florida finished with eight penalties for 92 yards, but it was the timing of those mistakes that exacerbated things.

The SEC is packed with unforgiving opponents and the Gators cannot afford to shoot themselves in the foot against the likes of Texas and Georgia. Hopefully, Sumrall can find a way to instill a little more discipline into his team as they dig deeper into the thick of the conference schedule.

GOOD : Duke Clark is legit, huh? Florida has two really good backs it can beat teams with — without needing a receiving corps. I'm always happy to see these performances come in big games. It leaves the "Yeah, but it was against a good Group of Four" argument a non-factor.

Florida can run it down a top-5 team's throat and drop a 50-burger. Do something about it. This Sumrall guy was serious about winning now. The Gators are officially a team to talk about after that dominant win.

BAD : Doing the "bad" in these always suck because I don't feel like anyone was really bad. You don't punish a good cornerback for not getting thrown at, right? Chambliss threw for 300, Alexander caught 135, and they have no run game without Lacy. This is what playing the opponent looks like.

UGLY : Injuries aren't good. We saw Bryce Lovett, Vernell Brown III and a few other players show discomfort on the sides. Bailey Stockton being awake is a good sign, but that was a rough hit he took.

GOOD : Jadan Baugh has legitimately positioned himself to be the best running back in the country. After today, the All-SEC back has double-digit touchdowns this season after a hat-trick performance. He also added 142 rushing yards to his season total, helping establish the Gators as one of the conference's premier teams.

BAD : The defense continues its bend-don't-break, don't-break mentality after giving up 28 points to Ole Miss. Florida's defense was able to force two fumbles and an interception in their victory over the top-five team.

UGLY : This isn't necessarily ugly, but Aaron Philo looked very pedestrian. The Gators' starting quarterback completed less than 70% of his passes but did miss a couple of throws that could have pushed the lead further in this ranked matchup.

articles.title: Why Shane Beamer yelled at South Carolina star Dylan Stewart on sideline vs Alabama
articles.summary: South Carolina football coach Shane Beamer ripped into Dylan Stewart, his star edge rusher, on his way back to the sideline vs Alabama.
articles.body:
After the third touchdown of the first half for Alabama , a replay showed South Carolina football coach Shane Beamer laying into his star edge rusher Dylan Stewart.

The ESPN broadcasters said it appeared that Beamer was yelling at Stewart for slowly walking off the field or not getting off fast enough.

On that same drive, Stewart was called for a roughing the passer penalty and it ultimately ended with a 42-yard touchdown from Ryan Coleman-Williams.

Beamer walked over with Stewart to the sideline and then Stewart's position coach Deion Barnes came over to Stewart as well.

ESPN sideline reporter Taylor McGregor reported that there was a lot of yelling between the Gamecocks players, but encouraging yells with the intention of playing better, she said.

South Carolina trails 21-3 on the road with five minutes left in the second quarter.

articles.title: Valkyries expect Wings to put up fight in first-round playoff series
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries went 3-0 against Dallas this year, but the team is expecting the Wings, who won 27 games, to be far from a pushover in a best-of-t...
articles.body:
San Francisco City Hall lit its pillars violet and the Salesforce tower illuminated purple basketball playing silhouettes across the LED display on its tip.

The city is ready for the Golden State Valkyries ' playoffs to begin. The Valkyries appear ready to rock, too.

The Valkyries will play the seventh-seeded Dallas Wings in the first round, having won their season finale to avoid a first-round matchup against Caitlin Clark and an Indiana Fever team that boasts one of the more effective offenses in the WNBA.

The Valkyries are in a different spot than they were in 2025. Getting their bearings in their inaugural season, the Valkyries stumbled injured, not able to play on their home court due to a scheduling conflict, into the postseason as the No. 8 seed pitted against top-seeded Minnesota .

They were swept last year, but came back in 2026 the No. 2 seed - not the newbie underdog - and will carry lessons from last year into Sunday's Game 1 against Dallas. But this year's team is not only coming back with experience as a franchise, but experienced players.

Kiah Stokes , Cecilia Zandalasini and Kayla Thornton have all won titles. And Golden State is coming back with prized acquisition and All-Star Gabby Williams , who has helped further solidify this team's defensive prowess.

"Any time you get playoff experience, it helps," said Veronica Burton , who was a key part of the Valkyries' run last year. "Understanding that the stakes are much higher and you don't have much time between games.

"You lose one, and the pressure is on more so and you understand what's at stake, but you can't afford to hold onto anything or wait until the next possession or game. You got to leave it all out every time you step foot on the floor."

The Valkyries went 3-0 against Dallas this year, but the Wings are no treat. They've orchestrated a massive turnaround since last season, when they fell to the lottery pick, got the first overall pick and selected Azzi Fudd - who was out most of the season and will miss the playoffs with a knee injury.

Dallas is in the playoffs on the back of a turnaround season headed by star Paige Bueckers , their first-round pick in 2025 who averaged 20.9 points per game, fifth best in the WNBA. The Wings won a total of 19 games over the 2024 and 2025 seasons but were 27-17 this year.

Golden State's strategy going into the series will at least somewhat mimic how it beat Dallas in the regular season: Pressure and physicality against the Wings' Bueckers, Jessica Shepard and Arike Ogunbowale .

That means picking those primary ballhandlers up fullcourt and "making sure they're under duress," Williams said.

"Our energy has to be high defensively," Williams said. "We have to pick them up high. We have to be physical with them. You definitely can't relax because those players just need a little bit of space to get going. So just making sure we're on high alert."

The strategy has to kick to another level, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase added. One change the Valkyries noticed during film study in preparation for this Round 1 series is that Dallas coach Jose Fernandez is changing up sets to get Bueckers freer.

Golden State found success against the Wings partly by being able to limit Bueckers' playmaking, preventing her from getting to her spots and mucking up screens. A freer Bueckers complicates their strategy.

"That respect level has to be even higher," Nakase said. "Just because everyone raises their sense of urgency, their physicality. We studied, obviously, the film. There's a three-headed snake with Paige, Jess and Arike. But their role players are playing amazing as well. So just meeting them early, pressuring as much as we can. But on the same side we have to execute."

Homecourt advantage for the Valkyries is no small thing. The team sold out every game at Chase Center, where it was 17-5 this year.

The Valkyries are the first team in league history to make the playoffs in their inaugural season and now the first franchise to make the postseason in their first two years of existence. But Sunday will be the first time the Valkyries get to play a postseason game at Chase Center.

Last year, the presence of the Laver Cup at Chase Center forced the Valkyries to play their playoff home game against the Minnesota Lynx at SAP Center in San Jose.

"Everyone traveled to San Jose, so I really felt even last year that (SAP Center) was Ballhalla," Nakase said. "It was just a different arena. So, like I said, our fans travel. It's really important that they show up and show out because they never waver, Valhalla. So that teaches us. They don't waver, we don't waver. We're one unit."

Last year's playoff run felt more of a test run, in retrospect, Nakase said. Before Thursday's regular-season finale in Los Angeles , Nakase said she feels connected with her coaching staff compared to last year when everyone was still learning each other - how to communicate and strategize in a pinch.

"Last year, I felt like we were in survival mode a little bit, just because we're out three starters and we're kind of really pressing and reaching," Nakase said. "This year, we're calm, we're composed and I think we're really prepared this year."

Golden State's composure under duress was exemplified Thursday in Los Angeles when the Valkyries overcame a 16-point deficit to topple the Sparks on L.A. forward Nneka Ogwumike 's retirement night.

In the comeback, the Valkyries showed the kind of clutch playmaking and scoring a playoff team must wield in October. Burton kept them afloat, Kaitlyn Chen took matters into her own hands and Williams delivered the game-winning plays in a matter of seconds.

"Gabby is our closer," Nakase said. "You saw the last game, her going in and boom, hitting those two threes. But more importantly, how did she get into the flow better? She got two steals."

articles.title: Kings close out preseason with win over Ducks
articles.summary: The next time the Los Angeles Kings take the ice, points will on the line.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The next time the Los Angeles Kings take the ice, points will be on the line.

When Los Angeles travels to Colorado to face the Avalanche in the season opener on Wednesday night, it will mark the first time in 20 years that franchise icon Anze Kopitar , who scored 452 goals and collected 864 assists across 1,521 regular season games, will not suit up in the Black and Silver.

"He's a Hall of Famer, obviously, so it's tough shoes to fill," Alex Turcotte said.

Los Angeles closed out its fourth and final preseason game Saturday afternoon, defeating the Anaheim Ducks 6-2 at Crypto.com Arena behind a balanced offensive performance.

"That's the way you want to finish the preseason," Turcotte said. "We're looking forward to Colorado."

The opening period featured a back-and-forth affair, with Anaheim and Los Angeles each finding the back of the net twice. After Beckett Sennecke 's power-play goal gave the Ducks a 2-1 lead, Adrian Kempe evened the score with less than a minute remaining in the period, redirecting a pass from defenseman Brian Dumoulin underneath Ducks goaltender Lukas Dostal 's pad.

Kempe, who led the Kings in points last season with 73, liked what he saw from his team in the preseason finale.

"Offensively, defensively, everything was pretty solid tonight," Kempe said. "I think that's as good as you can get in the preseason."

Mats Zuccarello , the newest member of the Kings, put Los Angeles ahead early in the second period, burying a power-play goal off an assist from Artemi Panarin to give Los Angeles a 3-2 lead. The 39-year-old signed a one-year deal with Los Angeles in July after spending the previous seven seasons with the Minnesota Wild and could prove to be a crucial component to LA's power-play attack this season.

"He's (Zuccarello) so smart, Kempe said. "[It's] been impressive to watch him."

Los Angeles' power play was a major source of frustration last season, finishing in the bottom five of the NHL at 17.0%. If Saturday's performance is any indication, there could be reason for optimism.

Los Angeles converted twice on the man advantage against Anaheim, with Zuccarello and Erik Haula converting to help fuel the victory. After averaging just 2.68 goals per game last season, fourth-fewest in the NHL, consistent production from a top unit featuring Brandt Clarke , Quinton Byfield , Panarin, Kempe and Zuccarello could provide a significant boost to the Kings' offense.

Leading by one entering the third, the Kings took control with the help of strong period from the 25-year-old Turcotte. The center doubled the LA lead by tipping a Drew Doughty shot past Dostal before sniping a second goal top shelf to extend the lead to three.

"He's worked really hard to show what he can do," head coach Peter Laviolette said. "He's always been a highly skilled player."

Wednesday will mark the start of a new era for the Kings, with Peter Laviolette making his debut behind the Los Angeles bench. The 61-year-old becomes the 32nd head coach in franchise history and the seventh NHL franchise he has led as he enters his 24th year in the league.

Laviolette brings a wealth of experience to a Kings team entering unfamiliar territory without franchise icon Anze Kopitar. His 1,594 regular-season games as an NHL head coach rank ninth in league history, while his 846 wins rank sixth all time. Laviolette also has a Stanley Cup title on his résumé, guiding the Carolina Hurricanes to the championship in 2006. As Los Angeles turns the page, that experience could prove valuable as the Kings begin life in a post-Kopitar era.

Kopitar's presence in the Kings' locker room will undoubtedly be missed, leaving Los Angeles with the challenge of filling the leadership void left by its captain of 10 seasons. Fortunately for Los Angeles, the organization has another longtime cornerstone in Drew Doughty, who enters his 19th season with the Kings. The veteran defenseman was named the 15th captain in franchise history on Sept. 16

A two-time Stanley Cup champion, Doughty will look to carry that experience into his new role as Los Angeles pursues a sixth consecutive playoff appearance. The Kings have failed to advance past the opening round of the playoffs since their improbable 2014 Stanley Cup run, putting Doughty and a new-look Los Angeles team in position to push the franchise beyond its recent postseason struggles.

Los Angeles opens the regular season Wednesday on the road against the Colorado Avalanche , the team that swept the Kings in the opening round of last season's playoffs.

The matchup marks the second consecutive season the Kings and Avalanche have met in the season opener. The meeting sets the stage for an early test for Los Angeles as it begins a new era under Laviolette.

articles.title: Timberwolves Has Full Training Camp Roster, Several Players to Compete for Roster Spots
articles.summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves have made a plethora of moves over the past week or two to prepare for training camp, which opens next week. While most of the rec...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Timberwolves have made a plethora of moves over the past week or two to prepare for training camp, which opens next week. While most of the recent moves were made for their G-League squad, the Iowa Wolves, the Wolves added two players late last night to compete for the final roster slot on their 15-man roster.

According to Michael Scotto of Hoophype, Minnesota signed Drew Timme and KJ Martin to Exhibit 10 deals late last night. Scotto added that both players will compete for a roster spot during training camp.

Timme is entering his fourth NBA season after spending last year with the Los Angeles Lakers on a two-way deal. Timme is a highly skilled big man who is efficient in the post and an outstanding rebounder, and has developed into a real perimeter threat, splitting last season between the Lakers and the South Bay Lakers. He averaged 3.4 points and 1.2 rebounds over nine minutes of action with shooting splits of 57.6/44.0/55.6 for Los Angeles last year.

Martin has appeared in 309 NBA games over five seasons. Martin is an elite athlete who excels in transition and finishing at the rim. The 25-year-old spent this past season with the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association, averaging 8.0 points on 61.4% shooting from the field and 3.8 rebounds in 23 games.

2 Other Players Who Will Compete For Final Roster Spot

While Timme and Martin are the newest additions, Minnesota has a full training camp roster with Antonio Reeves and Norchad Omier also on Exhibit 10 deals.

Reeves is entering his third NBA season. The 25-year-old is an elite movement shooter who is efficient from deep, draining 1.1 threes per game over 54 NBA games at 40.8% from the 3-point line. He has flashed three-level scoring in the G-League and possesses outstanding size.

Reeves, the No. 47 pick of the Orlando Magic in 2024, was with the Charlotte Hornets last year on a two-way deal. While Reeves spent most of his time with the G-League's Greensboro Swarm, he did make 10 appearances with the Hornets — compiling 2.7 points in 7 minutes over those appearances, with shooting splits of 50/53.8/00.0. He spent this past summer with the Chicago Bulls .

Omier is entering his second professional season. Omier is a physical interior presence — at 6-7 and 248 pounds — with a high motor and thriving in transition and on the offensive glass. He is also solid defensively and on the defensive glass.

Omier, who went undrafted, split time this past season between the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Los Angeles Clippers . After starting the season with the G-League Cleveland Charge before signing a two-way deal with the Clippers. He ended up playing seven games with the San Diego Clippers and made six appearances for Los Angeles. Then this summer, he played for the Clippers, averaging 10.6 points on 58.3% shooting and 9.8 rebounds (5.0 offensive).

The Last Word on Timberwolves Camp Competition

Minnesota has completely retooled its roster this summer despite only adding five newcomers. By trading Julius Randle , Naz Reid , and Josh Green (late in the offseason), the Timberwolves were able to create some flexibility. As a result, the Timberwolves are $4.6 million below the second apron and can add a 15th player.

The Timberwolves' biggest remaining need is frontcourt depth. The Wolves could also use another shooter, with Donte DiVincenzo likely to miss the season , which is why Timme and Reeves project as the favorites for the last spot.

Timme is a true fit for the Wolves, as he can theoretically replace Randle given his scoring and passing skills. Timme possesses the size that the Wolves need on the interior, is outstanding operating at the elbows, and also has shown the ability to stretch the floor — which Rudy Gobert , Joan Beringer, and Rocco Zikarsky can't. However, defense is a major weakness for him.

Reeves is also an outstanding fit for the Wolves with DiVincenzo sidelined, as he gives them a catch-and-shoot sniper off the bench. But he doesn't do much else and is only average on defense.

Martin is better suited on the wing, but his athleticism, motor, and defensive ability allow him to guard down a position. He is an outstanding fit alongside Ball due to his vertical pop. So, if Timme shows he can't handle things defensively, it could open the door for Martin. Meanwhile, Omier is a Reid clone.

Timme, Omier, and Reeves are eligible for two-way deals. So, it is possible that if Zikarsky or Enrique Freeman impresses the Wolves during camp, they will be promoted to a standard contract. Thus, opening a two-way spot. On the same token, it is possible that Omier, Timme, or Reeves straight beat out Zikarsky, Freeman, or Zyon Pullin .

articles.title: New York's Cameron Young and New Jersey's Chris Gotterup team up for 2 US wins at Presidents Cup
articles.summary: Cameron Young and Chris Gotterup have similar backgrounds and playing styles.  “I think both of us, when in doubt, tee it up, hit it hard, go find it,” Young...
articles.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. (AP) — Cameron Young and Chris Gotterup have similar backgrounds and playing styles. They often play together when they are home in Florida.

The connection between the two helped keep the United States within striking distance of the International team in the Presidents Cup on Saturday.

"I think both of us, when in doubt, tee it up, hit it hard, go find it," Young said.

That strategy worked quite well as Young and Gotterup combined for two big points for the Americans after a disastrous Friday session against the Internationals. They beat Nick Taylor and Corey Conners 2 and 1 in fourballs and then routed Sungjae Im and Adam Scott 6 and 4 in foursomes in the afternoon at an increasingly difficult Medinah.

Playing with different partners, Gotterup dropped his first match on Thursday and Young lost on each of the first two days. But together they helped the U.S. trim its deficit to three points going into Sunday's singles matches.

"We're different, but we play similar styles of golf in the fact that if he hits it in the rough, I've been in, like, a similar position where we're not going to be in the fairway all the time just with how far we hit it," Gotterup said. "It's not uncomfortable in the spots we put each other in.

"We just have a connection through being from the Northeast and just playing golf, and then being from the same area, I think it helps."

Young, 29, was born in Scarborough, New York, and Gotterup, 27, grew up in New Jersey. They both played college golf, Young at Wake Forest and Gotterup at Rutgers and Oklahoma. They also hit the ball a long way.

They both drove the 354-yard, par-4 No. 4 in their fourballs match on Saturday, and Young made a 39-foot eagle putt to give the Americans a 4-up lead.

"That's just such a strong pairing," U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker said. "The way those guys hit it, the way those guys played, they vibed today. They were having fun. Cam was making putts. Chris was hitting it a mile. It was fun to watch. Those guys have a long career in front of them in these things, and I'm glad we found that pairing."

Young has two wins this year and is ranked No. 3 in the world. Gotterup has three victories and is ranked No. 7.

The duo got off to a fast start in each of their matches. They were 5 up through seven holes while downing Im and Scott in the shortest match of the week.

"We played a fourball match the other day at home, and he beat all of us on his own ball," Young said of Gotterup. "Anytime you've got someone with that gear to go like that, it's exciting. I've seen him do a lot of crazy stuff with the golf ball. It's fun to watch, and he's very, very talented."

articles.title: 5 things you might've missed in UND's 42-35 win over Indiana State
articles.summary: Sep. 26—TERRE HAUTE, Ind. — The Fighting Hawks held off a late rally from Indiana State on Saturday in a 42-35 victory at Memorial Stadium. Here are five thi...
articles.body:
Sep. 26—TERRE HAUTE, Ind. — The Fighting Hawks held off a late rally from Indiana State on Saturday in a 42-35 victory at Memorial Stadium.

Here are five things you might've missed during the game.

UND needed to battle through injuries offensively.

The Fighting Hawks started the game without tight ends Haydn Stay, Aidan Behymer and Hunter Kallstrom.

Then during the game, UND lost offensive linemen Liam Becher and Ayden Teeter. Late in the game, the Fighting Hawks also lost wide receiver Caleb Goodloe.

Becher was wearing a protective boot on the sideline after his injury. Former offensive line starter Caleb Olson entered the game after Becher's injury.

"I haven't been able to sit down and talk (to the trainers) yet," UND head coach Eric Schmidt said. "Goodloe I'm a little bit concerned about just listening to where our trainers are at right now. I'm not sure with Becher at all. Teeter has been battling an ankle from all the way at our first scrimmage in the fall.

"Some important people there. Those are some guys who have been really, really productive for us here this year and in the past, too."

Goodloe finished with six catches for 62 yards.

UND was able to build its original lead in the second half with big performances from quarterback Jerry Kaminski on third down.

Kaminski's best play of the day came on third-and-8 from the 50 in the third quarter. With pressure in the backfied, Kaminski rolled to his right, and a split-second before stepping to the sideline, he fired a pass to Korey Tai, who tip-toed the sideline for a 22-yard pickup. Four plays later, Kaminski ran a quarterback sneak into the end zone for a 35-21 lead.

Early in the fourth quarter, Kaminski was facing third-and-10 from the UND 33. He was able to find Caleb Goodloe up the sideline for a 28-yard gain.

One play later, Kaminski went deep to Cameron Weir, who caught his second touchdown of the game for a 42-21 lead with 9:37 left.

"I saw the safety roll down, and I knew it was a one-on-one with a corner, and I was like 'I've got to win,'" said Weir, a first-year transfer from Washington State. "This is my ball. Jerry threw it, and I just made a play."

Starter Avery Dixon didn't travel to Indiana State with an injury, so the Fighting Hawks started Grant Tylutki, who had been playing the nickel position previously.

UND also utilized Jy Martin at safety. Martin, a starter all of last season, hasn't played this year as he seeks an additional season of eligibility from the NCAA.

Martin received a temporary restraining order against the NCAA from the Grand Forks Count District Court earlier in the week, allowing him to play against the Sycamores.

"Rusty," Schmidt said of his impressions of Martin so far. "I just think he's got some work to do to get back to where he was at. I did think it was good to get him back out there, just give him a taste. He knows he's rusty. He's coming off, and he's like, hey man, I've got to do a better job there."

The only running success UND's offense found against the Sycamores was through Kaminski, who finished with 18 carries for 86 yards and two touchdowns.

Griffin Broderick, who started the season as UND's fourth option in the backfield, led the running backs with 11 carries for 39 yards.

Charles Langama had five carries for 19 yards, while Matt Lawson had six carries for 7 yards.

"We still have to run the football better," Schmidt said. "A lot of different guys playing (on the offensive line) today. I feel like the guys up front have got to be able to do a better job of being on the same page. We'll look at the tape. Our backs have some competition there, too."

Schmidt said Langama was limited by a shoulder injury.

UND's special teams were a struggle against Indiana State.

Kicker Kenten Laughmann missed a 40-yard field goal with UND looking to go up 17 points in the second half. He also kicked two balls out of bounds on kickoffs late in the game, allowing the Sycamores to start at the 35.

UND also failed to capture an onside kick despite calling a timeout before the play to make sure the team's hands team was on the field.

On the onside kick, wide receiver Deng Deng sat back on the bounding ball and Indiana State was able to snare the kick.

UND punter Luke Silvernale also averaged just 41.8 yards on five punts, despite a 56-yard punt among the attempts.

articles.title: Dante Moore injury: Oregon QB takes scary hit to head, carted off field, put in ambulance
articles.summary: Oregon football quarterback Dante Moore took a scary hit to the head as he was sliding and lay prone on the ground for several minutes before being carted of...
articles.body:
The play happened with just over 10 minutes in the second quarter. Moore scrambled on a play and when he took a slide, USC defender Desman Stephen II hit him late. A flag was thrown and Moore was not immediately moving but his body was twitching as the Oregon support staff rushed to attend to him.

Oregon players immediately got in the faces of USC defenders and a near brawl broke out as the officials and coaches tried to break it up. A targeting penalty was called on Stephen and offsetting unsportsmanlike conduct flags were assessed to both teams for the scuffle after the moment.

Moore stayed on the ground for an extended period of time and didn't appear to be moving. The Oregon team huddled together while Moore was attended to, and USC quarterback Jayden Maiava came over to check on him.

After minutes of being down, Moore was put onto a stretcher and when he did, the entire Oregon team rushed to him to check on their star player. After he was taken off the field, Moore was put inside a waiting ambulance. Moore didn't appear to move and he didn't give a thumbs up to the crowd.

It's unknown what exactly happened to Moore, but he appeared to suffer a serious head injury and will be heading to a nearby hospital to be evaluated.

It's a devastating injury for Oregon as Moore is one of the best quarterbacks in the country. He could have been a top five pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but decided to stay for the chance to lead the Ducks to their first national championship on a highly talented roster.

Moore was 8-for-10 with 77 yards prior to the injury.

At the time of the pass, a blanket could have been thrown over the top three riders, but that was occasioned by catastrophe for the teenager Mayla Herrick.

Herrick earned the holeshot and then gave up the top spot to Cannon until that rider slipped off the track. In the chaos, Hodges took the lead with Herrick pressing hard.

Cannon regained her composure and rode through the field to challenge for the win in the 10-minute, plus one lap race featuring the fastest women in Motocross.

Herrick was one of the fastest riders on the track until she moved to the right to pass Hodges for the lead on Lap 3. Herrick clipped a Tuff Blox and crashed hard in the sand.

That incident brought Cannon back into the fight.

Mikayla Nielsen and Jordan Jarvis graced the fans with one of the best battles of the evening, battling for fourth and fifth. Jarvis took the position on the last lap.

articles.title: No. 25 UH avoids a scare, pulls away from pesky Georgia Southern in second half for win

STATESBORO, Ga. - They scored on a flea-flicker and then caught the University of Houston napping on an onside kick.

They kept exposing a UH pass defense that has been a weak link during the first month of the season.

They chanted, "Whose House? Our House!" inside Allen E. Paulson Stadium.

And for part of the first half Saturday, Georgia Southern had the No. 25 Cougars on the ropes.

With the game tied, UH answered with four straight touchdown drives and pulled away for a 42-28 non-conference victory over Georgia Southern.

UH's offense produced at least 440 yards for the fourth time this season and scored touchdowns on six of seven drives.

"We feel like we haven't reached our full potential," said wide receiver Koby Young, who caught his fourth touchdown of the season.

You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter .

Conner Weigman threw for 239 yards and accounted for six touchdowns for the Cougars. UH did not punt until 6 ½ minutes left in the game.

The Cougars (3-1) won in the first visit by a Power Four team to Statesboro and in the return of coach Willie Fritz, who won a Sun Belt title in two seasons at Georgia Southern .

"I knew nobody in the state of Georgia when I came here," said Fritz, who coached the Eagles from 2014-15. "I remember when they wanted me to take the job. They said, 'Do you have any questions?' I said, 'Yeah, why don't want to hire me?' I came in here and these people embraced me. I just love them. They are good, good people."

UH (3-1) appeared in control early, capitalizing on an early turnover to jump out to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter. Georgia Southern fumbled on the fifth play of the game, setting up Weigman's 5-yard run. Weigman added a 22-yard touchdown pass to Young.

Georgia Southern (1-3) answered with a trick play, as quarterback Max Johnson took the flea-flicker and tossed a 40-yard pass to Alex Taylor, who made the touchdown grab while falling backward with a defender in tight coverage.

Georgia Southern coach Clay Helton, a former UH quarterback in the early 1990s and son of former coach Kim Helton, caught the Cougars off guard with an onside kick on the ensuing kickoff. Eagles kicker Blake Ford bounced a high kick that Josh Dallas recovered 11 yards downfield, setting up an eight-play, 54-yard drive that was capped by a 2-yard run by Ty Cummings to tie the game at 14.

UH closed out the first half with a pair of touchdowns - a 1-yard run by Weigman and 2-yard catch by Traville Frederick Jr. Tight end Patrick Overmyer set up the go-ahead touchdown with a 47-yard catch to the Eagles 4. Re'Shaun Sanford II had 42 of his career-high 120 rushing yards on the final touchdown drive before halftime.

Trent Walker, a transfer from Oregon State, had his best game as a Cougar with six catches - matching his entire total in the first three games - for 83 yards, including a 23-yard touchdown catch on the opening drive of the second half. All six of Walker's catches resulted in first downs.

"That kind of put it out of danger," Fritz said of scoring to begin the second half.

Weigman completed 17-of-22 passes for four touchdowns, one shy of his career high.

Amare Thomas added an 11-yard score early in the fourth quarter, his nation-best ninth straight game with a TD catch.

Taylor had a 23-yard catch in the third quarter, his second touchdown of the game, to pull Georgia Southern within 35-21. Georgia Southern closed within 42-28 on a 5-yard TD catch by River Helms with 8:20 left. After forcing a UH punt, the Eagles converted a fourth-and-4 near midfield. Faced with another fourth down attempt, Johnson's pass was incomplete to seal UH's victory.

UH's pass defense struggled again, allowing seventh-year quarterback Johnson, who played two seasons at Texas A&M , to complete 26-of-38 for 284 yards and three touchdowns. Taylor had six catches for 119 yards and two touchdowns.

"There was three or four times we had a chance to shut the door and make a play and we didn't quite do it," Fritz said. "That happens. Sometimes there is going to be a game we're relying on the defense like crazy."

articles.title: Class topper, wooden gun, Nano rides: How Shapath Bharadwaj found his way to the Asian Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: If not a shooter, Shapath Bharadwaj could have been seen dealing with deadlines, just like his journalist father, S Raju.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: If not a shooter, Shapath Bharadwaj could have been seen dealing with deadlines, just like his journalist father, S Raju. In a house where books and newspapers were always around, there were expectations that Raju's son would follow the same path.Shapath did well in studies too. He was a class topper from childhood and a favourite among his teachers. But somewhere in his mind, he had already chosen a different path - shooting.Shapath fell in love with shooting at an early age - nine - after watching his elder brother train. His father initially thought his younger son, who was so good at academics, simply wanted to try the sport out of curiosity. He did not know that the sound of gunshots would draw his son in at such a young age.Years later, that passion has taken Shapath to the Asian Games, where he will represent India in trap shooting.The startShapath was nine when he first saw his elder brother, Shrey Bharadwaj, train at a shooting range. He had already seen guns at home and heard conversations about competitions, but this was different. For the first time, he heard the gunshots, saw clay targets being hit and watched them break into pieces.He was hooked.The nine-year-old went home and told his father, "Papa, I also want to become a shooter. I also want my own gun."Instead of laughing off his son's demand or ignoring it as a child's passing interest, Raju decided to help shape his dream.The 'dummy' shotgunShapath kept asking for his own gun. His father eventually approached a carpenter, showed him a real shotgun, and asked him to make a dummy one that looked exactly like it."I still remember. The first thing the carpenter said was, 'The police will take me to jail. How can I make this?'" Shapath recalls with a smile."I was so happy when my father gave me that wooden dummy gun. It was my first gun, and I still have it at home. My brother helped me use it for dry training at home. That was a special day in my life," he says.The journey beginsFor Shapath, studies and shooting soon started going hand in hand.A schoolboy in his uniform, sitting in the back of his Nano while his father drove from Meerut to the shooting range, with his mother helping him study during the journey, became a regular sight.The journey from Meerut to the Karni Shooting Range in Tughlakabad could take three-and-a-half to four hours one way, depending on the traffic and road conditions. The family made the trip four times a week."There were big cars at the shooting range. My father used to bring me in a Nano. People used to come in big cars, but that never bothered me or affected me. I was just happy that I was shooting. I was taught from childhood that you cannot judge a person by the car they come in," he says.Those long journeys also taught him lessons that went beyond shooting."That routine taught me discipline. You have to sleep on time, wake up on time and finish your work on time. Even while travelling, I was doing my school work. I was studying in the car," he says.The Asian Games callHis route to the Asian Games team was built on a series of strong performances on the international stage.At the 13th International Grand Prix in Porpetto, Italy, in 2016, Shapath won gold medals in both the individual and team events in double trap. He followed that with a silver in the team event at the 8th International Shotgun Cup in Orimattila, Finland.In 2017, he continued his medal-winning run. He won bronze in the individual event at the ISSF World Cup in Porpetto before helping India win gold in the team event at the 9th International Shotgun Cup in Orimattila. Later that year, he won another gold in the team event at the ISSF World Championship in Moscow, Russia.In 2019, he won bronze in the individual trap event at the Italy Open Green Cup in Todi, Italy.In 2022, he won gold in the team event at the ISSF World Championship in Osijek, Croatia, and bronze in the team event at the ISSF World Cup in Lima, Peru. In 2023, he won silver in the junior individual trap event at the 15th Asian Shooting Championship in Changwon.The Asian Games call came while he was competing at the ISSF World Cup in Almaty, Kazakhstan."I was playing in the World Cup in Almaty at that time. My coach came to me and told me about my selection. That was when I found out that I had made the Asian Games team," he recalls.'It's an opportunity'Excitement or pressure? Shapath prefers another word - opportunity."For me, it is more of an opportunity. To represent your country, to give everything for your country and your flag, and to work hard. Whenever we go to an international competition, the first thought in my mind is that we are wearing the Indian flag. There is pride in representing India, but there is also a feeling of responsibility," he says."The target is the same. I just have to follow my process, follow my basics and execute them. One target at a time, till the end," he says.For the boy who once travelled for hours from Meerut in a Nano, studied in the back seat of the car and did dry training with a wooden dummy gun, the Asian Games is another step in a journey that began at the age of nine.And according to Shapath, that journey has only just begun.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
