articles.title: Chess Olympiad 2026: Can India retain their gold medals on final day in Samarkand?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The decision hour is upon us. The countdown has begun.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The decision hour is upon us. The countdown has begun. The winners of both the open and women's sections of the 46th Chess Olympiad will be decided later today. Do India have a chance to retain their gold medals? Certainly, perhaps more so for the open team, less so for the women's side, though there is still a route to a minor miracle there too. Either way, the fate of both Indian teams is no longer entirely in their own hands. They will have to win their own matches and then hope the teams above them slip up elsewhere.On Saturday, in Round 10, India delivered exactly the kind of statement win they needed, beating Uzbekistan's second team 3.5-0.5 in Samarkand. Praggnanandhaa got things going with a win over Jakhongir Vakhidov, Nihal Sarin cruised to victory after his opponent, Mukhammadzokhid Suyarov, blundered straight out of the opening, and Gukesh added a smooth win of his own with the London System against Ortik Nigmatov.Arjun Erigaisi was the one to leave something on the table. He had a completely winning position against Abdimalik Abdisalimov but couldn't find the finish, settling for a draw instead.Uzbekistan's own top team made no such mistakes, crushing Armenia to stay perfect. That result leaves the standings finely poised heading into Sunday's final round. Uzbekistan lead outright on 18 match points, with India alone in second on 17. Germany, Ukraine and Hungary make up the chasing pack, all on 16.Open section: India dominant, but the door isn't fully openThe equation for gold is straightforward, even if the odds require some help. Uzbekistan face Ukraine, a side in decent form themselves after beating China in the penultimate round, with Vassily Ivanchuk and Roman Dehtiarov among those capable of causing an upset.India, meanwhile, take on Hungary, a team missing a bit of firepower at the top (Richard Rapport has been playing solid rather than spectacular chess) but dangerous further down the order, where Gleb Dudin has been in the form of his life.If India beat Hungary and Uzbekistan lose to Ukraine, the gold is India's outright. If India win and Uzbekistan draw, the two sides finish level on match points, and it comes down to the Sonneborn-Berger tiebreak, which is essentially a measure of the strength of the teams you've beaten. It's not a tiebreak India are likely to win; without many big-margin victories across the tournament, India would probably fall short of Uzbekistan's score even in a shared-points scenario.If Uzbekistan win regardless of India's result, they clinch the title. What is virtually certain, though, is a win against Hungary will assure India of at least a silver.Women's section, a much tougher askThe picture is considerably tighter, and less favourable, in the women's section. India needed something special against China on Saturday to keep their own gold hopes fully alive, and for a long stretch it looked like it might slip away entirely.Koneru Humpy and Divya Deshmukh drew their games on the top two boards, before Vantika Agrawal, despite reaching a promising position, was undone by a fine piece of play from Lu Miaoyi and lost on board three.That left everything resting on Savitha Shri against Zhai Mo on board four.It very nearly didn't come off. Playing white, Savitha's 19.Bg5 turned out to be the moment the game nearly slipped away. Zhai's reply, 19...Nxd4, grabbed a pawn while simultaneously attacking White's queen, setting up a forced sequence of captures (20.Bxd8 Nxc2 21.Bxc2 Raxd8) that saw both queens and a minor piece come off the board. When the smoke cleared, Savitha was a pawn down, in exactly the kind of position that punishes a single loose moment.What followed instead was one of the gutsiest fightbacks of the tournament. Savitha dug in through a long rook-and-knight middlegame, gradually improving her pieces and refusing to let the earlier deficit rattle her, before finding an outside passed pawn on the a-file that became her lifeline.She played the position very patiently, move after move, all the way up the board, and once it reached a7 with nothing left to stop it, Zhai had no choice but to resign.It kept India's 2-2 draw against China intact, and with it, India's gold-medal hopes alive, if only just. That result leaves China on top with 18 points, Kazakhstan second on 17, and India sharing third with Poland and Vietnam on 16.The final-round pairings make India's route to gold a genuinely narrow one.China face Vietnam, a good side themselves, with their best individual threat likely to come from their fourth board, while Kazakhstan take on Poland, a fixture India know something about, having lost to Poland themselves earlier in the tournament, which is precisely why a Kazakhstan slip there feels realistic.India, for their part, play Georgia, who have a strong line-up on paper, led by Nana Dzagnidze, Bella Khotenashvili, Lela Javakhishvili, and Meri Arabidze on Board 4 for Sunday's encounter.On the other hand, India have fielded Humpy, Divya, Vantika, and Savitha, with Vantika rested. They have chosen to keep it the same on the final day.For India to have any realistic shot at gold, three things need to happen on the same day.They first need to beat Georgia, and by a healthy margin if possible to boost their own tiebreak score; China must lose outright to Vietnam (a draw would still take China to 19 points, out of India's reach even with a win); and Kazakhstan must draw or lose to Poland. It isn't impossible; but asking three separate results to fall the right way in the same round, with China needing to lose rather than merely drop points, is exactly the kind of outside chance that needs a touch of the miraculous.Individual medals in the mix tooBeyond the team standings, both Indian teams have strong individual contenders heading into the final round.Gukesh, on 8.5 points from 10 games, is a serious contender for individual gold on his board, and will face Hungary's in-form Gleb Dudin, who himself sits on seven from nine, in what could be one of the most closely watched individual match-ups of the day.READ ALSO: Father quit Singapore job, pawned jewellery to fund chess dream: Olympiad-bound Savitha Shri's storySavitha Shri, unbeaten through nine games and sitting on 8.5 points herself, is in an equally strong position for an individual medal of her own, regardless of how the team competition ultimately resolves.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: One point short in 2018, Trap Shooter Ahvar Rizvi gets his Asian Games chance eight years later
articles.summary: In 2018, Ahvar Rizvi missed India's Asian Games selection by one point.
articles.body: In 2018, Ahvar Rizvi missed India's Asian Games selection by one point. He was competing in Double Trap then, an event in which he had established himself as one of India's promising young shooters. At the World Championships in Changwon that year, Rizvi won the junior Double Trap title. The Asian Games place, though, went elsewhere."I missed the Asian Games by one point," Rizvi told TOI Sports. "I was very sad because there is a competition once every four years, and it is a big competition. You miss that, so then I didn't understand what to do."There was another problem. Double Trap was subsequently removed from the international programme, leaving Rizvi to move to Trap in 2019."I struggled a lot when Double Trap was closed," he said. "I had been in the team continuously for six or seven years, and then suddenly I was out of the team."Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleSeven years later, Rizvi is back in an Indian team for the Asian Games. This time, in Trap. The 26-year-old from Mahalgaon, Meerut, is preparing for his first appearance at the continental Games after making India's 2026 men's Trap squad alongside Kynan Chenai and Shapath Bharadwaj - the bronze medallist at the Juniors, in which Rizvi had claimed gold in 2018."It took me seven or eight years to get here," Rizvi said. "So this is my first international trap event and my first Asian Games. So I am feeling very proud. I am going to play for India. I will keep India's flag high there."From a Double Trap gun to a borrowed Trap gunRizvi had started shooting because shooting was already part of the family. His father, uncles and cousins shot. As a child, he used air guns before asking his father if he could take up shotgun shooting. His father initially felt he was too young for the recoil of a 12-bore."There was a lot of recoil in the 12-bore. I was small and very thin at that time, so my father told me not to do it yet," Rizvi said.He went to his uncle instead. "When I came here, I qualified at the state level. When I reached home, all the family members were standing there with flowers for me. They welcomed me."He then qualified for the pre-nationals and nationals. He still did not have his own gun. His cousin Raiyan Rizvi let him use his. "I didn't have a gun, so my cousin Raiyan, whom I just told you about, used to let me use his," he said.Rizvi was too young to have a licence. The gun was also physically large for him. "When I was competing in the nationals, the gun was bigger than me," he said. "My cousin used to stand behind me. When the recoil came, he would push me back. So he used to stand behind me to support me."That was the beginning. The Indian team came next, followed by the junior world title in Double Trap in 2018. Then the event disappeared and Rizvi had to learn Trap."I kept doing it, but my coach, Vikram [Singh Chopra] sir , who was always with me and supported me, never told me that I had shifted from double trap and that I couldn't do it," he said. "He always told me that I would be able to do it."It took years before Rizvi felt he understood the new event. "After two or three years, I started to understand what trap was."The scores still did not immediately follow. He missed selection by a few points in 2024 and again in 2025. There was also a point when he stopped shooting."There was a point in between when I quit because it was not happening," Rizvi said. "But when I represented India, I thought I would do it in the future."The borrowed gun that took him to the Asian GamesThe equipment was another part of the rebuild. Rizvi's old Double Trap gun could not simply be carried over to Trap. He eventually got a Trap gun from teammate Lakshya Sheoran, the Asian Games silver medallist, and used it in nationals and trials for a year."Although I have a trap gun, this gun is not mine. This is my friend Lakshya’s gun. He is an Asian Games silver medallist," Rizvi said."So he has given me this gun. I have been competing in nationals and trials with his gun for a year." Rizvi now has his own stock, made in Italy and adjusted for competition."The stock is mine, and I have adjusted it for competition," he said. "I am seeing a lot of improvement since I changed my stock." The equipment was still being fine-tuned when he was preparing for the Asian Games."Vikram Sir, when we were in Italy for the World Cup, and I got my stock set up," Rizvi said. "I was a little worried about my equipment, but now I just have to focus 100 per cent on what I have to do."His 2026 international results show the work is still in progress. He finished 39th in Trap qualification at the Almaty World Cup with 115 and 47th at Lonato with 118. At Almaty, Rizvi and Pragati Dubey finished 23rd in the mixed team event with 130. The selection trials, though, gave him the opening he had been waiting for.And this time, there was no one-point calculation to make."I never thought that if I had got that one point at that time, it would have been different," Rizvi said of 2018. "It was just that I didn't get it then, so I was a little sad. Then I put it behind me and started again."Away from the range, he is in the fieldsHis life away from shooting is rather different from what the range might suggest. Rizvi's family has been involved in shooting for years, but farming remains part of his everyday life."Ahvar Rizvi is a normal person. He is a son of a farmer, and if there is no shooting, he is in the fields with his father and elder brother," he said.The Asian Games, though, have been the thing he has been waiting for."We are in this game, and everyone's expectation when we go to an event is to bring gold," he said. "Gold will not come just because we are in the team. We have to work hard."There will be nervousness. Rizvi expects that. "There is excitement and nervousness when we play a match. But the main thing is to control it."His way of controlling it is to talk to his coach. "When I talk to my coach whenever I get nervous, I get a lot of relief and I stay focused."His first Asian Games comes after the competition he missed in 2018, the event he lost in Double Trap, the years spent trying to make sense of Trap and a selection process that finally went his way. He does not spend much time looking back."I went back and never looked back," he said. "Now it is 2028, and the Olympics are coming. Now I have my eyes on it."For Nagoya, though, his instructions are simpler."We get thoughts before shooting. We think when we are competing. Those thoughts come, but stopping them is very important.""If the target is going to be left, let it come. But we have to break. We have to hit the target.""Never give up. So this is my thought."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Oregon Coach Dan Lanning Announces Dante Moore Injury Update After USC Win
articles.summary: The No. 20 Oregon Ducks secured a massive 41-27 victory over the No. 12 USC Trojans on Saturday night.However, they were led by second-string quarterback Dyl...
articles.body:
The No. 20 Oregon Ducks secured a massive 41-27 victory over the No. 12 USC Trojans on Saturday night.

However, they were led by second-string quarterback Dylan Raiola , who entered the game after starter Dante Moore suffered a scary head and neck injury when a USC defensive back hit him very late as he slid to the ground.

Moore had to leave the field on a stretcher before an ambulance took him to a nearby hospital for further evaluation.

A positive report during the game revealed that Moore could move his extremities.

Dan Lanning Gives Update on Moore's Status

After the game, while speaking to the media, Oregon head coach Dan Lanning gave a short but important injury update on Moore's status based on the latest information he had received.

"Certainly the energy changed whenever Dante got hurt," Lanning said, via Nick Hamilton . "We had a lot of guys on the sideline that were emotional in that moment, including myself, but right now indications are that he's in recovery, so I don't want to speak too soon, but he is moving, he has the ability to move, so we'll continue to assess him, but I don't want to speculate on further thoughts on that until we have more information on him."

After spending each of the last two seasons at Nebraska , Raiola elected to transfer to Oregon knowing there was a good chance Moore would return for another season and he'd serve as the second-string quarterback.

Yet, he did it anyway with the idea of learning, getting into a system, and eventually taking over the reins in 2027, while also serving as an extremely formidable backup if called upon, which he showed Saturday night.

He completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards, two touchdowns, and no turnovers. He accomplished all of this in basically a half and some change, helping Oregon move to 3-1 on the season.

articles.title: IND vs WI: Three Sachin Tendulkar records that Virat Kohli can break during India vs West Indies ODI series
articles.summary: Discover the three iconic Sachin Tendulkar records Virat Kohli can break during the India vs West Indies ODI series, from 15,000 runs to home tons.
articles.body:
India star Virat Kohli returns to international action against the West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram.

Kohli remains unbeaten in two ODI innings at Thiruvananthapuram, a venue that could suit a record-breaking knock.

A few records are within his reach that he could potentially breach during the West Indies series.

Virat Kohli vs Sachin Tendulkar: 3 major batting records at stake in India vs West Indies ODIs

Virat Kohli is back in action in India colours, and he will be aiming at a handful of Sachin Tendulkar milestones, as the Men in Blue take the field at the Greenfield International Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram against West Indies on Sunday afternoon.

Against West Indies specifically, Kohli's numbers already read like a highlight reel with 2,261 runs across 43 matches and 41 innings, at an average of 66.50, studded with nine hundreds and 11 fifties.

If we take a look at his overall ODI career, Kohli sits second only to Tendulkar's staggering 18,426 runs, with 14,941 runs of his own from 314 matches and 302 innings, averaging 58.59 with 54 centuries and 79 half-centuries, including a best of 183. That puts him just 59 runs shy of becoming the second batter in the format's history, and the second Indian, to cross the 15,000-run mark.

Moreover, Kohli is also two centuries away from breaking Tendulkar's mark of 42 international hundreds on home soil. And there's a third home record in his sights as well: Tendulkar's tally of 6,976 ODI runs at home, compiled across 164 matches.

Kohli isn't far off at all, sitting on 6,867 runs from 130 matches and 127 innings, at an average of 62.42, with 27 hundreds and 36 fifties, leaving him just 110 runs short.

What is Virat Kohli's record in ODIs in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala?

Virat Kohli boasts an unblemished ODI record at Greenfield International Stadium, having never been dismissed in his two outings at the venue.

He debuted at the ground on November 1, 2018, finishing unbeaten on 33 against the West Indies.

His crown jewel in Thiruvananthapuram arrived on January 15, 2023, when he plundered an undefeated 166 against Sri Lanka. It is the venue's all-time highest individual score across all international formats.

Form-wise, nothing is suggesting a slowdown either. In six innings so far this year, Kohli has piled up 384 runs at an average of 64.00 and a strike rate above 106, including one century and three fifties.

These are numbers that suggest these milestones could tumble sooner rather than later, possibly even during this very series.

There's something almost poetic about Kohli chasing down Tendulkar's records at a ground where he's never once been dismissed, as it feels less like coincidence and more like a venue tailor-made for a big statement.

What's most striking here isn't just the proximity to these numbers, but how effortlessly current his form looks while chasing them; a strike rate above 106 in ODIs at this stage of his career suggests he isn't simply accumulating milestones; he's still playing attacking cricket.

Records against Tendulkar's name have always carried extra weight in Indian cricket discourse, given how untouchable many of his numbers once seemed.

Watching Kohli methodically close in on several of them in the same series, rather than one at a time, makes this stretch of matches exciting, regardless of how the results eventually shake out for either side.

articles.title: ‘This Is Illegal,’ ‘How Inexcusable Was This?’ — CFB Fans Question How SEC Refs Allowed Controversial Tennessee Onside Kick vs. Texas
articles.summary: Texas escaped with a dramatic 20-17 win over Tennessee at Neyland Stadium Saturday. The victory kept the Longhorns undefeated at 4-0, with their defense play...
articles.body:
Texas escaped with a dramatic 20-17 win over Tennessee at Neyland Stadium Saturday. The victory kept the Longhorns undefeated at 4-0, with their defense playing a major role in the matchup.

Texas' special teams unit, meanwhile, made a huge blunder in the game, allowing Tennessee to recover a controversial onside kick that could have turned the game on its head.

That kick became one of the biggest talking points of the weekend for a very different reason.

College Football Community Furious After Tennessee's Controversial Onside Kick vs. Texas

On the play in question, Tennessee punter Jackson Ross attempted an Australian-rules football-style drop kick on the onside kick.

Instead of placing the ball on a standard plastic tee, Ross held it in his hands, ran forward, and dropped it onto the turf before immediately kicking it as it bounced.

Texas wide receiver Ryan Wingo nearly secured the ball, but it came loose, allowing Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter to recover it at their own 49-yard line.

NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay later argued that the play should have been ruled illegal because Ross did not kick the ball from the 35-yard line.

"This is illegal on a kickoff. The ball must be kicked on the restraining line, the 35-yard line here. There is an exception for safety kicks, but not a kickoff," McAulay tweeted.

Many from the college football community also joined in the discussion.

"This was an illegal play. Has to be kicked from the 35-yard line. Exactly the 35. No exception in the rules," one user on X wrote.

"I was today years old when I learned this was a legal kick in the game I have spent my life employed by," Valor Christian Athletics head football coach Mike Sanford remarked .

The recovery gave Tennessee a chance to pull off a miracle comeback before a last-second Hail Mary was broken up in the end zone.

The fact that officials initially threw a flag before picking it up and awarding Tennessee the ball only added to the frustration among some fans.

"Interesting. However, not surprised the SEC officials didn't know this rule," one fan piled on.

"How inexcusable was this today? Once again getting away with a blatant right job, NCAA," another user added.

"Tennessee recovered an illegal onside kick at the end of the Texas game. But not even the refs could help them actually tie the game," the Bad Sports Refs account wrote .

The legality of Tennessee's onside kick is likely to remain a major talking point throughout the week.

However, from Texas' perspective, the win significantly strengthened its position in the College Football Playoff picture, as PFN's Playoff Meter shows the Longhorns' CFP chances increasing by 7.8%.

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes injury: Jorge Jesus describes Man United skipper’s condition as “worrying”
articles.summary: 1Bruno Fernandes is carrying a hip problem which has affected him for around three matches, with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus admitting that the Manchester U...
articles.body:
Bruno Fernandes is carrying a hip problem which has affected him for around three matches, with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus admitting that the Manchester United midfielder's condition is "worrying".

Fernandes has not trained at all ahead of today's Nations League clash with Norway and Portugal 's medical staff are due to assess whether he could feature, creating concern over his availability for United's busy October schedule.

United face a demanding October schedule

Manchester United are due to face Spurs on 10 October, Atletico on 13 October and Leeds on 18 October. The tight turnaround means any problem lingering beyond the international break would be crippling for United.

That situation comes with United already going through a difficult patch, winning just one Premier League game out of five and being knocked out of the Carabao Cup. Losing Fernandes now would remove the side's main creative influence at a point when consistency is badly needed.

The immediate priority, however, is determining the severity of the hip issue. No specific recovery time was given, so it remains unclear whether this is simply a case of managing his workload or a problem that could affect his return to club duty.

A Bola carried Jesus' update when the Portugal coach was asked about both Nuno Mendes and Fernandes before the Norway game.

Jesus said: "Nuno Mendes is not a major problem because he came off with fatigue and not an injury. If I want to, I can use him in the game, provided he gives me good feedback in training.

"The more worrying one is Bruno Fernandes because he played with a problem in his hip, but he really wanted to play. As you saw, he was not even at his usual level.

"We will see whether he is ready for the game and what the doctors say. He will not even train. He has been playing with that pain for around three matches. I have already spoken to him and I would prefer not to risk him, so that I can have him at 100 per cent for the game against Denmark ."

The comments confirm that Fernandes was playing with the same issue for United against Fulham and Brighton , when he came on as a substitute in the second half.

Fernandes remains difficult for United to replace

Jesus' description of Fernandes pushing to play despite the issue underlines the midfielder's willingness to make himself available. It also raises the question of whether continued involvement has prevented the hip problem from settling.

If Fernandes cannot immediately return for United, Michael Carrick's options in attack are dwindling. The head coach is already without Amad and Ben Sesko , so Mason Mount and Joshua Zirkzee are the only obvious alternatives in the number 10 role.

Another option would be to bring Carlos Baleba into the number six role, allowing either Kobbie Mainoo or Youri Tielemans to play further forward.

United supporters face an anxious wait. With three more Portugal matches in this international break, the national team's handling of the injury could prove crucial in whether Fernandes returns to Old Trafford fit and available or in need of an extended layoff.

Fernandes has played around three matches with hip pain.

Jesus said the midfielder would not train before facing Norway.

Portugal may rest him with the Denmark game in mind.

United have three fixtures between 10 and 18 October.

articles.title: Washington Huskies Offense Stumbles Again in 27-24 Loss to Minnesota Golden Gophers
articles.summary: The Huskies failed to overcome a slow start in their Big Ten opener against the Golden Gophers.
articles.body:
SEATTLE — The Washington Huskies football team looked unprepared and overmatched for most of its Big Ten opener against the Minnesota Golden Gophers on Saturday at Husky Stadium.

The Huskies fell to 3-1 with the loss. It was a disappointing result for a team that begun the year ranked 17th in the country and considered a potential darkhorse for the College Football Playoff.

"I think that all our goals are still in front of us," UW third-year quarterback Demond Williams Jr. said after the game. "We have a whole lot of ball to play, a whole lot of good teams to play still. For us, I think that we have to use this game as a learning lesson and, go into the next week with a clear state of mind."

Washington's secondary was without starting cornerbacks Emmanuel Karnley and Rahshawn Clark. Both were listed as game-time decisions in the final injury report and both suited up for pregame warmups. Clark was limited to his punt and kick return duties whereas Karnley was held out of the game.

The shorthanded secondary, and the rest of the UW defense, was unable to provide any answer for Minnesota's offense and third-year quarterback Drake Lindsey in the first half.

The junior signal-caller finished the first 30 minutes of the game 15-for-16 for 125 yards and three touchdowns. It was the first time in his career he had three passing in the first half. Lindsey finished the game 21-for-29 for 204 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

"I thought they did a good job, shout out to them, but we just got to be better making our plays," UW linebacker Jacob Manu said in a postgame interview Saturday. "I feel like they did a good job of, when we were showing different coverages, running the ball. We just got to make our tackles and make those plays."

The Huskies were only able to muster one touchdown in the first half.

That score came via a 16-yard touchdown pass from Williams to second-year wide receiver Dezmen Roebuck with 13 minutes, nine seconds left in the first half.

Washington kicker Tyler Robles connected on a 33-yard field goal with 1:56 left in the first half, which cut Washington's deficit down to 21-10. The game went into halftime with the same score.

The defense was able to put together a better showing in the second half and limited the Gophers to a field goal. That kick came with 54 seconds left in the third quarter and bolstered Minnesota's lead to 24-10.

Washington's offense was unable to award its defense's persistence. The Huskies had four drives on offense in the fourth quarter and only mustered one first total first down. The last drive of the third ended in Williams' second interception of the game thrown to senior Gophers tight end John Nestor.

That pick gave Minnesota the ball back in Huskies territory, but the visitors were unable to cash in.

The Huskies offense showed its biggest signs of life in the fourth quarter. On fourth-and-5 from the Gophers 15-yard line, Williams channeled former Seattle Seahawks quarterback Russell Wilson and extended the play before finding second-year tight end Baron Naone in the back of the end zone for a touchdown. That pass and the subsequent extra points cut Minnesota's lead to 24-17.

A field goal bolstered the Gophers lead back to 10 with just under seven-and-a-half minutes to go in the game, but Washington was able to muster one last scoring drive.

Williams scored on a 13-yard quarterback keeper with 1:53 left in the game, which resulted in the eventual final of 27-24.

Unfortunately for UW, wasted seconds ended up coming back to bit them.

Before Williams' keeper, the Huskies had the opportunity to run one play in the end zone before the two-minute timeout, which would have given the Huskies two timeouts and an opportunity to get the ball with just over a minute left if it got the defensive stop on Minnesota's last possession.

Washington was late getting the substitution on the field and the game clock ran to the two-minute timeout before Williams' touchdown run.

The Huskies were able to get the stop against the Gophers on defense and got the ball back, but there wasn't enough time left on the board for Washington to have a realistic chance to drive

"We wanted to get a certain red zone play in," UW head coach Jedd Fisch said after the game. " ... We wound up subbing, and the sub came in way too late. And with that, then they got the hold, another 10 seconds (off the clock). That's my fault. Certain personnel group that I wanted in the game for that play so we wound up having to call it after the two-minute warning."

The Huskies will be looking to bounce back in their first road game of the year against the Southern California (USC) Trojans at 4:30 p.m. PT on Oct. 3 at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Enes Kanter labels Cheryl Reeve unfit for WNBA amid latest transgender comments
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom has expressed his unfiltered views on Cheryl Reeve’s latest comments about transgender athletes. The Minnesota Lynx concluded the 2026 WN...
articles.body:
Enes Kanter Freedom has expressed his unfiltered views on Cheryl Reeve's latest comments about transgender athletes.

The Minnesota Lynx concluded the 2026 WNBA season with a stunning 86-66 win over the Indiana Fever .

While the dominant win prepares the Lynx well for the postseason, most fans paid attention to what head coach Cheryl Reeve had to say after the game.

Reeve clearly mentioned that supporting transgender athletes has been one of the biggest achievements of her life in 2026. However, this didn't sit well with former NBA player Enes Kanter.

Enes Kanter wants Cheryl Reeve to 'step down'

Kanter addressed Reeve's statement in a now-viral X post, where he demanded that the veteran coach step down as the head coach of the Lynx following her stance on transgender athletes.

"Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve should step down immediately. You can't lead women's basketball while refusing to stand up for women's sports.

"Can someone, for the love of God, please explain to her that: Protecting women's sports is not an attack on anyone's existence, nor does it erase a community," Kanter wrote on X .

He added, "Coach, if you truly mean what you just said, then put your hypocrisy aside and prove it by drafting me in the 2027 WNBA Draft."

On one hand, Kanter demanded Reeve's resignation, but on the other, he urged the coach to draft him in the 2027 WNBA Draft.

It seems like yet another desperate plea from Kanter to stay relevant in an attempt to revive his basketball career.

articles.title: Remontada Redux: LA Galaxy Score 3-2 Fightback Win
articles.summary: Los Angeles, Calif. -- A second-half LA Galaxy onslaught, powered by Joao Klauss' gift goal and a Justin Haak headed winner, powered LA to their second strai...
articles.body:
Los Angeles, Calif. -- A second-half LA Galaxy onslaught, powered by Joao Klauss ' gift goal and a Justin Haak headed winner, spurred LA to their second straight come-from-behind 3-2 win, this time at home.

It was also the first time the Galaxy has won two straight matches all year. And after last week's win over Minnesota in similar fashion, the signs are there that momentum is building for the G's.

"I think we're showing progress. The capacity to win games in some different ways, showing confidence, and being able to... we got ahead last week, then we went behind, then we came back to win, and then today we get behind two at home. We showed the resilience to come back and win," LA Galaxy Head Coach Greg Vanney shared with the Sporting Tribune.

"So again, I think we're showing progress, and why we are making progress, we're still finding, we're winning games, and that's what's most important down the stretch right now. Is that you win games."

It was a tale of two halves again in LA, as the hosts conceded right out of the gate in the fourth minute.

Colorado Striker Donavan Phillip was played in behind the Galaxy defense, beat Jakob Glesnes for pace, and kept his nerve to beat Galaxy Goalkeeper JT Marcinkowski for the 1-0 scoreline. Just moments later, Marcinkowski was tested again and kept the deficit at one with a point-blank one-on-one save.

In the week when the Galaxy starting goalkeeper signed a contract extension, Marcinkowski once again proved his worth by making two key saves when the Galaxy defense was in disarray. Time and again, the Galaxy #1 has kept his team in games this season, and his teammates have been vocal in their praise, with Haak calling him the "best and most consistent performer" on the team following the win over Colorado.

"No. You look at the quality of the team and look at the quality of that locker room. We have guys who played all over the world at the highest level, and I think what's really cool is that we're coming together at the right time," the shotstopper said post-Colorado.

LA Galaxy players celebrate what would be the game-winning goal from Defender Justin Haak (15) during LA's 3-2 win against the Colorado Rapids , Saturday, September 26, 2026, in Carson, Calif.

"I think there's been plenty of games you look back earlier in the year where it's just small details. We missed a pass here. We let in a goal there. But it seems to be that we're kind of we're clicking and we're ticking at the right moment. So no, I don't think so. I think if I thought I was the best player, I would probably be delusional. So, all I really want to do is just help the team."

Saturday night was no different, and Marcinkowski was his typical solid self. Unfortunately, his good play could not prevent Colorado's second.

More troubling still, it came virtually like the first.

After Paxten Aaronson was played in behind the Galaxy defense on the left, he was able to get the better of Lucas Calegari in the physical battle over the ball. Once beaten, the Galaxy backline could only watch as Aaronson finished the breakaway for the 2-0 score.

But whatever Greg Vanney's half-time team talk was, it worked.

LA came out with renewed vigor and immediately put Colorado under pressure with a high press designed to cause mistakes. A change in formation at the start of the second half produced a stifling Galaxy press that began to turn the game.

And after several close moments, LA finally made the breakthrough in the 54th minute.

The Galaxy made good use of Klauss' aerial presence with a well-worked play that saw a tantalizing cross played into the striker. Klauss hung in the air for the ball, but could not meet the service. But his momentum led to a Reggie Cannon own goal that put LA on the board with a 2-1 scoreline.

Klauss would then score the easiest goal of his career to level the game.

The big striker latched onto Rapids Goalkeeper Nicholas Hansen's errant pass and only had to guide it into the net to tie the match at two-all. From there, the Galaxy comeback felt inevitable.

"The crowd and the players and the energy in the stadium was as in sync tonight as it has been, I feel like, for maybe two years. And so I felt like that was huge, and I felt like that's part of what brought the energy that we were able to come back," Vanney said while praising the home support.

His goalkeeper agreed. Marcinkowski described the home support as "powerful" and didn't doubt that a third goal was coming.

"I think the crowd really brought the energy, and you could feel it," Marcinkowski said of the Galaxy faithful. "You could feel that the third goal was going to come as soon as we scored the second one. It was just more of a matter of time."

Eight minutes later, the Galaxy completed their improbable fightback.

After sustained attacks, LA won a corner kick. Haak rose to meet Robert Taylor's inswinging cross to score his first Galaxy goal and the potential game-winner.

After a shaky start to the game, Haak and center-back partner Glesnes were then able to see the match out along with the rest of the backline despite the Rapids pressing hard for the equalizer.

In a match with huge playoff implications, the Galaxy took everything a direct playoff rival threw at them and came out on top. The slow start should worry Galaxy fans, but the finish should give them heart.

Now the Galaxy is in the thick of the postseason hunt.

The victory moved the Galaxy level on points with Colorado at 36, where they sit just one place behind the mile-high team in eighth in the Western Conference.

With a two-week break before a massive match against St. Louis City , the Galaxy's playoff fate is in their own hands.

"I think we're starting to see the pieces really coming together," Haak shared in a post-match press conference. Despite the good moment and the goal, he counseled calm.

"We can't get ahead of ourselves. We have to keep putting the work in and training. This is just three more points at the end of the day, and we still have work to do to qualify for the playoffs, and then keep going from there."

articles.title: Biggest win of our careers: Manush Shah & Diya Chitale on Asian Games bronze
articles.summary: Before the Asian Games started, not many gave Manush Shah and Diya Chitale a chance of winning a medal for India. While they are ranked World No.
articles.body: Before the Asian Games started, not many gave Manush Shah and Diya Chitale a chance of winning a medal for India. While they are ranked World No. 8 in mixed doubles currently, table tennis powerhouses like China, Hong Kong, Japan and South Korea were in contention too, and their recent form didn’t inspire much confidence. However, Manush and Diya rose to the occasion when it mattered the most, beating the World No. 4 team of Doo Hoi Kem and Wong Chun Ting in the quarterfinals to secure a historic bronze for India. This is only the second time India have won a TT mixed doubles medal at the Asian Games. Sharath Kamal and Manika Batra won bronze in 2018.The duo spoke to us from Japan about their historic feat.‘It doesn’t get bigger than this’Manush: It’s an amazing feeling because we had not managed to do well in really big events so far. So, both of us were very motivated to win the quarterfinals and add to India’s medal tally. It doesn’t get bigger than this; as a team, it’s certainly the biggest win in our careers. I spoke to my family in Vadodara, and they said they are proud of me. Massimo Costantini, our (Team India) head coach, has seen the struggle and played a big role in us staying mentally strong, which helped us a lot. Even when we were not winning, he was always there for us. I dedicate the medal to him. We are staying on a cruise ship for the Asian Games, which is a first for most of us. While there were some issues related to travel, we tried to adapt to the conditions and stay fresh and positive. It helped me stay in a good mental zone and perform well for India.Diya: I am very happy right now because it is our first win in such a big multi-sports event. It’s a very proud feeling and I want to thank my parents and all my coaches for their constant support. Emotionally, it has been a tough time for me because I lost Peter Engel, my coach since 2015, just a few days ago. I owe everything to him and whenever I had any doubts, he was just a phone call away. I wish he was around to see this medal. I dedicate my bronze medal to him.‘We always had self-belief’Manush: Asian Games is one of the toughest challenges in our sport, but once the draw was out, we were expected to reach the quarterfinals. We prepared well for the Hong Kong challenge and knew that we had to take our chances. I am glad we could execute the plans well. Even against the Olympic champions in the semifinals, we fought hard. Although we lost, we learnt a lot. The team event was tough and although we lost against South Korea, all three Gujarati players (Manush, Manav Thakkar and Harmeet Desai) put up a tough fight. I wish we had done better in men’s doubles (Manush and Manav).Diya:Before the start of the Asian Games, while we knew it was going to be a tough challenge, we always had self-belief. While we did not get the desired results as a team in the last couple of months, we knew we had a chance if we played to our potential. While we had lost our previous matches against the World No. 4 team, the last two matches were really close. This time, we played aggressively right from the beginning, fought for every point, and it worked.‘We contribute to each other’s strengths’Manush: Diya’s control is superb, and my power is good, so we complement each other well as a team and contribute to each other’s strengths. We try to play to our strengths and win points as early as possible without going much into the rallies.Diya: Manush and I started playing together as a team in 2023. We have had some amazing results and beaten some top teams so far. He is a very attacking player, and I enjoy playing alongside him. While this is a big win, this is just the beginning. Our biggest dream is to do well for India at the Olympics, but we want to take it one tournament at a time.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Nadie lo cuenta, pero los tiradores enrasados de los coches son cada vez más habituales por esta razón
articles.standfirst: Las manetas ocultas de los coches modernos responden a un cálculo de ingeniería aerodinámica clave para reducir la resistencia al aire
articles.summary: Las manetas ocultas de los coches modernos responden a un cálculo de ingeniería aerodinámica clave para reducir la resistencia al aire
articles.body: Cada vez más a menudo, subirse a un coche implica agarrar una maneta que está enrasada en la puerta, y que emerge para que tiremos de ella. El invento no es nuevo y ya hace años que hay coches en el mercado con esta solución. Quizá tú seas de los que piensas que es un bonito detalle estético que hace que la carrocería parezca más moderna. Pero la verdad es que, en la mayoría de los casos, este sistema no se monta para que el coche parezca más chulo. La razón está en el aire, que actúa como un muro invisible que el coche necesita atravesar de manera constante. Cuanto menos salientes tenga la superficie del coche, menor esfuerzo requiere su motor y menos energía o combustible gasta, y las manetas tradicionales sobresalen de la chapa varios centímetros, haciendo que se rompa la fluidez de la corriente lateral. Ahora bien, ¿se rompe mucho o se rompe poco esta aerodinámica? Pruebas realizadas en túneles de viento demuestran que las manetas enrasadas consiguen reducir el coeficiente aerodinámico (el famoso Cx) entre 0,005 y 0,015 puntos, teniendo en cuenta que un coche actual puede tener un coeficiente de 0,25. Esta merma parece diminuta a simple vista, pero en el diseño aerodinámico actual cada milésima cuenta como un triunfo, y más ahora que están proliferando los eléctricos y a muchos aún les genera ansiedad su autonomía. Comprenderás mejor la importancia de la aerodinámica si te decimos que, a velocidades legales de autopista, más del 70% de la energía del coche se puede destinar a vencer la resistencia del aire (depende de con que fuerza y dirección sople, claro). En ese escenario, limar medio punto equivale a liberar al motor de un lastre invisible. Por ponerlo en cifras, y hablando de los coches eléctricos (que son los que más las emplean), esa modesta mejora aerodinámica se traduce en una ganancia de entre 5 y 10 kilómetros extra de autonomía, dependiendo del coche. Se trata de un margen adicional que puedes agradecer en viajes largos, además de una ayudita para que cada marca trate de ofrecer más autonomía que las marcas rivales. ¿Significa esto que los tiradores enrasados resultan igual de importantes en los coches con motor térmico que en los eléctricos? La respuesta indica que la reducción de la resistencia al aire es idéntica en ambos casos. Pero en la práctica, su impacto es diferente. En un coche térmico de gasolina o diésel, la mayor parte de la energía del combustible (en torno al 60% o 70%) se pierde en forma de calor a través del tubo de escape y del radiador. Además, la parte delantera de estos coches necesita parrillas de refrigeración abiertas para enfriar el motor por medio del radiador, lo que genera bastantes turbulencias. En ese contexto, arañar unas milésimas de resistencia en las puertas ofrece un beneficio real en el consumo, tal vez unas décimas. Pero el resultado global queda eclipsado por la propia ineficiencia del motor de combustión. En un coche eléctrico, sin embargo, se aprovecha más del 80% de la energía almacenada en las baterías y el frontal carece de esas enormes parrillas propias casi de un Word Rally Car. Al tener una superficie en general más esculpida, cualquier pequeño saliente como la maneta de una puerta supone un porcentaje mayor del arrastre total. Por eso, aunque en un coche térmico ayuda a gastar menos combustible, es sobre todo en los eléctricos donde se convierte en una prioridad para bajar el consumo y aumentar la autonomía. Así que, aunque veas que quedan muy bonitos, el verdadero motivo está en la batalla contra el viento. Y esa es una batalla para la que cada vez más fabricantes quieren afilar sus diseños.

articles.body:
The 2026 BMW Berlin Marathon often promises fast racing conditions. The 2025 rendition saw World Record Holder Sabastian Sawe run 2:02:16, while Rosemary Wanjiru claimed victory in the women's race with her 2:21:05.

At the 2026 Berlin Marathon, Tigst Asefa will go after the Women's World Record.

3:50a ET - The Runners Have Crossed the Halfway Point

The men's lead pack still remain close together. Erick Sang, Selemon Barega, Andamlak Belihu, Gemechu Diriba, Shura Kitata and Asefa Boki have gone through the first half of the race in 1:01:01. Assefa is on world record pace. She crossed the halfway point in 1:04:57. The makes her projected finish time 2:09:53 and would be a few seconds under the current world record.

Sadly, Esther Pfeiffer dropped out of the race at 13km. It is unclear what has happened, but she been on pace of the women's German national record. 3:30a ET - Assefa Continues to Widen Her Gap at the Front

She lines up on the course where she set what was the outright women's marathon world record in 2023 (2:11:53) - she still holds the Berlin course record and the women's only marathon world record of 2:15:41 from London this past April. She enters as the clear favourite. Behind her: 2025 Berlin champion Rosemary Wanjiru, Bedatu Hirpu, Dera Dida, Zeineba Yimer, Bosena Mulatie, the list goes on. Esther Pfeiffer is targeting the German women's national record. Fourteen women in the field have run 2:25 or faster. As for the men, Gabriel Geay heads the men's field with a 34-second gap on the next-fastest entrant. articles.title: Is Australia v South Africa on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Springboks clash
articles.summary: Everything you need to know as the two sides clash in Perth
articles.body:
Australia and South Africa continue their busy international seasons with a one-off clash in Perth.

The Springboks are back in action just two weeks on from the conclusion of their Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series with New Zealand, and confidence is high after a 3-1 success.

Rassie Erasmus uses the opportunity to rotate in places in a week that has served as useful preparation for next year's World Cup, with the defending champions due to play a pool game and likely round of 16 tie in the Western Australia city.

The Wallabies , meanwhile, have made an encouraging start to life under Les Kiss and will hope to build momentum with a statement success before taking on the All Blacks twice next month.

Australia vs South Africa is due to kick off at 10.45am BST on Sunday 27 September at Optus Stadium in Perth.

Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on Sky Sports +, with coverage from 10.35am BST. A live stream will be available via Sky Go.

articles.title: Should Ohio State have let Texas score? And angry fans are good entertainment. Mailbox
articles.summary: Readers give their thoughts on Ohio State football, the Blue Jackets and other topics.
articles.body:
Have more comments, questions? Reach out to me at bwhite1@dispatch.com . Letters are lightly edited for clarity.

Mr. White : I laugh when I see reporters and former coaches when they say, "I would have let Texas score in the final minutes of the game to give OSU more time to mount a comeback." Coach Day made a decision which turned out to be not good.

Looking back in time, hindsight, is always 20-20 vision or better. Further, letting Texas score with one minute and one timeout remaining still does not guarantee an OSU score.

To Lauri : Analytics aside, such a predicament is difficult for a coach who has to explain to his defense why he had zero faith in it stopping an opponent. If the Buckeyes win, the defensive players and staff shrug and accept it. If they lose, it's one unhappy bunch. Decisions such as those, on a big stage, are why Day gets paid the big bucks.

To the editor : I love, love, love when Ohio State loses. Now, don't get me wrong. I'd rather see the Buckeye win. But there is nothing quite as entertaining as the aftermath of an Ohio State loss.

That's when the trash-talking fans come crawling out of the woodwork and into the Sports Mailbox. Fire coach Day! He can't coach! He can't call plays! He doesn't know what he is doling! Apparently, Ryan Day just fell off the turnip truck and wandered into Ohio Stadium. The controversy after a loss makes great reading.

Games like Kent State, where Ohio State wins a laugher, don't produce much excitement afterward. Everybody shrugs, says "Go Bucks!" and moves on.

But let Ohio State lose? For the next week, Columbus becomes one giant coaching staff. Everybody knows which play should have been called, which player should have been in the game and, of course, who should be fired.

So, yes, I want Ohio State to win. But when they lose, I grab my coffee and wait for the Sports Mailbox. That's when the real game begins.

Brian : Whenever Ohio State does lose a football game, I am reminded of my favorite quote by Theodore Roosevelt applauding the man in the arena and criticizing the critic on the sideline, which is worth looking up, and I wish also to remind people that among major college coaches with more than five full years on the job, only Knute Rockne had a better winning percentage. And remember Day has done this with today's postseason format which provides for many more games against other top-ranked schools, which previous generations did not have to struggle with.

See photo of Blue Jackets preseason opener against Red Wings

To Brian : I don't always watch the most irrelevant franchises in professional sports, but when I do, I prefer the Columbus Blue Jackets . Stay thirsty, my friends.

To Steve : How irrelevant? This week, USAT Today published a story titled "Which NHL teams could make postseason after missing last season?" Writer Mike Brehm listed the Panthers , Capitals, Sharks, Devils and Maple Leafs. Then, under "Other teams to watch" were the Predators, Blues and Islanders. Not a good early sign for the local squad.

articles.title: Ravens-Cowboys by the numbers: 7 statistical matchups to watch in Rio
articles.summary: Seven stats explain Baltimore’s rushing advantage, Dallas’ efficient passing game and the third-down battle in Brazi
articles.body:
After clearing up any issues with the field at Maracanã Stadium, Baltimore and Dallas are a little over 24 hours from kicking off what could be an explosive, high-scoring matchup. The clearest advantage for the Ravens over the Cowboys lands in the rushing attack. Baltimore has produced strong rushing numbers through the first two weeks. Dallas has allowed opponents to run effectively. That advantage matters, but seven numbers show why the Ravens must also contain Dak Prescott and improve on third down.

1. Ravens rushing offense: 155 yards per game

Baltimore has rushed for 310 yards through two games. Derrick Henry has 212 yards and four touchdowns, giving the Ravens a reliable starting point if they continue to keep him involved after halftime.

2. Cowboys rushing defense: 173.5 yards allowed per game

Dallas has surrendered 347 rushing yards. If Baltimore can exploit that weakness, it can create manageable downs for Lamar Jackson while reducing Prescott's opportunities.

3. Cowboys rushing defense: 5.0 yards allowed per carry

Dallas's problem is both efficiency and volume. Giving Henry five yards at a time would let Baltimore stay in the run game without waiting for a long breakaway play.

4. Cowboys rushing offense: 67.5 yards per game

Dallas has only 135 rushing yards through two games. Baltimore's defense has allowed 83.5 per game , suggesting the Ravens can make Prescott carry much of the offense if they tackle well.

5. Dak Prescott: six touchdown passes, one interception

Prescott has thrown for 454 yards while completing 73.8% of his attempts. Even a successful Baltimore rushing day will not matter enough if Dallas answers quickly through the air.

6. Cowboys offensive third downs: 15-for-22

Dallas' 68.2% conversion rate shows how well it has extended drives. The Ravens have allowed opponents to convert 11 of 25 third downs. Getting Dallas into third down will be only half the job.

7. Cowboys defensive third downs: 17-for-25 allowed

Opponents have converted 68% of their third downs against Dallas. Baltimore's offense is seven-for-18, or 38.9%, through two games. If the Ravens improve that rate in Brazil, they can turn their rushing advantage into longer drives and points.

The numbers favor Baltimore's ground game, but they do not decide the game by themselves. The Ravens must convert that edge into sustained possessions, then prevent Prescott from undoing that work in a few throws.

articles.title: Area seniors finish up high school golf careers at Franklin Regional
articles.summary: State berths elude Bloomington area competitors, who still have solid days at The Legends to end season
articles.body:
Bloomington North head girls golf coach Harrison Carmichael was standing on the 18th green at The Legends during Saturday's Franklin Regional, when it hit him hard. As each Cougar took their turn on the last hole, Alli Rensi, Annika Lowinger, Sadie Woodring, Mira Bruce and Kate Johnson, their high school careers were coming to an end.

And all Carmichael could think about was the incredible amount of work they had put in over four years, to go from a team finishing eighth at sectional with a 434, to one capable of finishing eighth at regional.

"From Kate to Alli, they really did work hard as a group," Carmichael said. "It was odd having all seniors. Normally, you're on the 18th saying, 'One or two are graduating and the rest are back.' But none of them will be back.

"So it was a somber 18th green. But we knew we did the best we could. And we knew we came a long way from where we were."

North shot a 392, 18 shots better than last year. Bruce, who birdied No. 8, went 46-47 for a 93, while Johnson had three pars on the back 9 for a 45 finish with a 95 total. Woodring shot 101, Rensi 103 and Lowinger 108.

"I was very proud of them," Carmichael said. "I can't ask for better. They didn't play the way they wanted to. Every single one, if they were honest, would say that.

"I think on the drive home and afterward, most of the conversation was about how much they've grown, Mira and Kate were shooting (138 and 116) as freshmen at sectional, so they've shaved a ton of shots off their scores. That's something to be proud of. They worked hard, all of them did and they left the program better than they found it."

State-ranked teams Center Grove (315), Floyd Central (337) and Franklin (339) advanced. Martinsville was sixth at 355. Olivia Alvey of Center Grove was medalist with a 71. It took an 82 to advance as an individual. Just two of the individual qualifiers from sectional broke 90.

Edgewood's Libby McElhinney, who was at regional last year with the Mustangs, shot a 100, six shots better than last year. Bloomington South's Silvia Walker fired a 105 and Owen Valley's Jacklyn Wheeler had a 109, getting off to a rough start on the back 9, but came home in 47.

In the Terre Haute North Regional at Hulman Links on Friday, Eastern Greene's Maddie Sylvester shot a 116.

McElhinney finished up her day with her second par to go with seven bogeys.

"She had a few bad holes that put a damper on what she was trying to do today," Edgewood coach Garry Lee said. "The course was in good shape, a bit damp. I had her play a combination of the golf and black tees at Cascades to get her used to the length.

"She played well in spots and struggled on a few holes, which is The Legends. It's tough for anybody. But overall, she had a pretty good senior season. Winning conference and playing really well at times."

Like the five Cougars, Walker capped her senior year with one last round at regional.

"Silvia had some inconsistency in her ball striking today but putted well," South coach Jim Southern said. "It was my great pleasure as her coach to walk along and coach Silvia today as she played her last round of her high school golf career for Bloomington South.

"Silvia handled setbacks well and she gave it her very best today on a tough and long course set up. I'm proud of her not only as a golfer, but also for the great person she is. It has been my pleasure coaching her for the past four years and she is going to be greatly missed on this team."

articles.title: “They had better ideas” Tarik Muharemovic discusses his exit from Juventus
articles.summary: Tarik Muharemovic is another success story from the Juventus Next Gen team who is now doing well away from the club, despite having been a potential option f...
articles.body:
Tarik Muharemovic is another success story from the Juventus Next Gen team who is now doing well away from the club , despite having been a potential option for their defence.

Juventus has struggled to find space for some of the best products of their Next Gen team in recent seasons. The club sold Muharemovic to Sassuolo in the summer of 2024, while also including a significant sell-on clause in the agreement.

The defender went on to star for Sassuolo in Serie B as they secured instant promotion to Serie A. He then produced an impressive first season for the club in the Italian top flight, further demonstrating his quality at senior level.

Muharemovic reflects on Juventus departure

His form last season led to speculation that Juventus wanted to re-sign him from the black and greens. However, Muharemovic eventually moved to Leeds United in the last transfer window, bringing his time in Italy to an end.

The defender remains grateful for the years he spent developing at Juventus, although he cannot explain why the club never gave him an opportunity in the first team despite his performances and potential.

The Bosnian has now spoken about his time coming through the ranks in Turin, explaining his perspective on his departure and his current situation at Leeds.

Speaking about his time at Juventus, Muharemovic said, as quoted by Calciomercato :

"Huijsen and I leaving Juve? They had better ideas and knew why. Now I'm really happy to be at Leeds and in the Premier League and not somewhere else. My focus is here and I just want to forget those early years. I spent five years in Italy, we all know it's a country specialising in tactics and defence. Tactically, it's the best place to grow."

His journey from the Juventus Next Gen ranks to Sassuolo, followed by a move to Leeds United, represents a significant progression in his career. While Juventus did not ultimately provide him with a first-team opportunity, he has continued to develop and establish himself at senior level.
